items.body_text:
Putin claims that Ukraine has no ‘antidote’ to Russia’s new jet-powered drones. Kyiv has already shown it can shoot them down, but doing it at scale could cost billions.
Speaking to reporters on the sidelines of the Cultural Forum, Vladimir Putin said Ukraine was seeking an “air ceasefire” out of weakness — especially because it feared Russia’s new jet-powered drones. The Russian president believes Kyiv has no “antidote” to these weapons. They are dangerous, but they lack the chief advantage of the earlier “Geran” drones: low cost. Developing defenses against the faster drones will also be expensive for Ukraine. Here is how the latest turn in the technological arms race could drain — and is already draining — both countries’ budgets.
What exactly was Putin talking about, and is he right?
An “air ceasefire” would mean a mutual halt to strikes on energy and transport targets behind the front lines. Putin believes Kyiv made the request solely because its infrastructure is vulnerable: “Apparently, they particularly need us to stop striking with our modern ‘Gerans.’ At least for now, they have no way to counter them — no antidote.”
By “modern ‘Gerans,’” Putin apparently means a new generation of drones that could more accurately be called small cruise missiles. These jet-powered aircraft are indeed nearly impervious to the layered defenses Ukraine built against older drones. Russia fielded large numbers of the new models from the start precisely because the old ones had become ineffective.
Jet engines have made the new weapons several times faster than their piston-powered predecessors. But that advance came at the expense of the older “Gerans’” main advantage: Estimates suggest the new models cost several times as much to produce.
Still, Kyiv is not entirely without an “antidote.” Ukraine has the technological capacity to build effective defenses. Paying for them is a harder problem.
Why did the old ‘Gerans’ stop being effective?
The Russian military received its first jet-powered drone in early 2025. It was essentially a standard “Geran-2” fitted with a small Chinese Telefly JT80 turbojet engine in place of its piston engine. The modified drone was named the “Geran-3.” Its speed roughly doubled, reaching 300–350 kilometers per hour (about 185–220 miles per hour), compared with its predecessor’s 150–180 kilometers per hour (about 95–110 miles per hour). Its range and payload — its warhead — were smaller, however.
The jet-powered version was developed in response to Ukraine’s increasingly effective air defenses. By then, Kyiv had deployed an effective interception network built around electric-powered interceptor quadcopters. Those drones were connected to a network of sensors: radar; acoustic sensors that located “Geran-2” drones and tracked their direction of flight by the distinctive sound of their piston engines; and optical and infrared sensors that could detect passing aircraft by day and night.
The main source is less than fully reliable: statements from Ukrainian military intelligence and the Security Service of Ukraine. The agencies give detailed accounts of their successes against Russian drones and of the new equipment Russia is using. Ukrainian intelligence officials have an obvious stake in the conflict and are engaged in information warfare.
There is also more objective evidence: photos and videos of downed aircraft and their parts, including engines; videos of interceptions by air defenses; and visual confirmation of the strikes themselves. Russian media outlets and military personnel have also shared technical details of the new weapons, though they, too, have a stake in the outcome. Taken together, this material gives a general picture of the new equipment and how it is being used.

items.title: Russia attacks Kyiv again with missiles and drones, sparking fires at an educational facility and the roof of a five-story apartment building
items.summary: Russian forces attacked Kyiv with missiles and drones overnight on September 29, Ukraine’s Air Force said. Several districts were hit, Mayor Vitali Klitschko said.
items.body_text:
Russia attacks Kyiv again with missiles and drones, sparking fires at an educational facility and the roof of a five-story apartment building
Russian forces attacked Kyiv with missiles and drones overnight on September 29, Ukraine’s Air Force said. Several districts were hit, Mayor Vitali Klitschko said.
In the Solomianskyi district, missile “debris” fell into the courtyard of a residential building. One of the buildings at an educational institution was hit, sparking a fire. Klitschko also said an administrative building at an infrastructure facility was hit. He did not identify the educational institution or the facility.
In the Pecherskyi district, a three-story nonresidential building caught fire after the attack. In the Holosiivskyi district, the roof of an apartment building caught fire as a result of “falling debris.”
”One person was injured in the Holosiivskyi district, according to Ukraine’s State Emergency Service. Rescuers evacuated 10 people from the damaged building.
In the Bucha district of the Kyiv region, a Russian drone strike set a private home and the roof of a neighboring building on fire. Two people were taken to hospitals.
Russian forces have struck Kyiv both day and night for several days. On September 28, a building belonging to Ukraine’s National Academy of Sciences was among the sites hit, and a fire broke out there. According to Kyiv authorities, two people were killed and 26 injured in Monday’s attacks. Eight of those injured remain hospitalized.

items.title: Russian pizza chain Dodo Pizza says hackers breached its systems and may have accessed customer data
items.summary: Dodo Pizza said hackers attacked its IT systems and may have stolen some customers’ data.
items.body_text:
Russian pizza chain Dodo Pizza says hackers breached its systems and may have accessed customer data
Dodo Pizza said hackers attacked its IT systems and may have stolen some customers’ data.
The attack took place on September 27–28. The company believes the hackers may have accessed some customers’ names, addresses, phone numbers, email addresses, dates of birth, and order details.
“We don’t store payment data — it’s safe,” the company said. It said it had already notified Roskomnadzor of the attack. The hackers have been blocked from accessing Dodo Pizza’s data, and the company is conducting an internal review.
Baza, a Telegram channel close to Russia’s security services, said the hackers had obtained data on 68 million Dodo Pizza customers in various countries, along with their order histories for the past 15 years.
Dodo Pizza is a Russian pizza chain. As of fall 2026, it had more than 1,527 pizzerias in Russia and 27 other countries.

items.title: Dmitri Shostakovich at 120: How the icon drew on Bach, jazz, and cinema to create his own musical language

items.title: Severed genital, grinder in room: What happened to Premanand Maharaj's disciple
items.summary: Deepak Lodhi, a follower of Premanand Maharaj, died after falling from the Gau Kripa Kunj Ashram. Forensic experts are examining a grinder found in his room for fingerprints and possible connections to his injuries. Lodhi sustained several injuries, including fractures and an amputated genital. The investigation is focused on determining how and why Lodhi fell from the fourth floor.
items.body_text:
AGRA: A grinder was found in the room of Premanand Maharajâs disciple Deepak Lodhi, whose private parts were found severed after he fell from the fourth floor of an ashram in Vrindavan, adding a new twist to the police probe into his death.
Forensic experts are now examining the grinder to determine whose fingerprints may be present on it, while investigators are trying to establish whether Lodhi inflicted the injury himself or whether someone else was involved.
The post-mortem report indicates that Lodhi sustained injuries at multiple places, including deep injuries to the head, a fractured rib and a fractured leg bone. It also records the presence of an amputated genital along with the body.
According to the report, Lodhi had a stitched wound involving 14 stitches on the head, a wound on the chin and another stitched wound near the genitals. The report also notes a fracture underlying one of the injuries.
Police are examining the circumstances surrounding the injury to Lodhiâs private parts, which is now a key part of the investigation.
The grinder mystery
Police have recovered a grinder from Lodhiâs room and, with the help of a forensic team, are trying to determine whether it was used in connection with the injury.
Investigators are examining the fingerprints on the machine as part of their effort to establish who handled it.
The probe is also focusing on whether Lodhi could have inflicted the injury on himself or whether another person was present or involved.
Post-mortem records multiple injuries
The post-mortem findings show injuries to the head, chin, leg and chest area, besides the injury to the private parts. The report records a haemorrhage in the scalp region and a hairline fracture with haematoma.
It also mentions fractures in ribs on the left side of the chest.
The body was noted as being present in two parts in the post-mortem report, with the amputated genital listed separately.
Police are examining the post-mortem findings alongside forensic evidence and the circumstances in which Lodhi fell from the fourth floor of Gau Kripa Kunj Ashram near Varah Ghat.
Police probe fatal fall from ashram
Vrindavan DSP Sandeep Singh said police first received information that an injured man had been admitted to Sarvodaya Hospital on September 25.
"A report was received that a person had arrived at Sarvodaya Hospital in an injured condition and was admitted on Sept 25. Upon taking cognisance of this information, an immediate investigation was conducted, and it was learned that his name is Deepak Lodhi alias Rasik Dulari Sharan, who is a resident of Jabalpur. He was residing at Guru Kripa Kunj Ashram associated with Kali Kunj. Information has come to light that he committed suicide by jumping from the roof of the fourth floor. In this regard, the forensic team and Vrindavan police station team were immediately sent to the spot. Evidence has been collected from the scene by the team, and the Vrindavan police station team is carrying out the probe," he said.
Fourth-floor fall followed by multiple injuries
Deepak Lodhi, alias Rasik Dularisharan, 25, a native of Jabalpur in Madhya Pradesh, had allegedly jumped from the fourth floor of the ashram around 10.30am on September 25.
Other seekers rushed him to hospital, where doctors declared him dead. His body was later sent for post-mortem examination.
Lodhi had moved to Vrindavan in 2025 to follow Premanand Maharaj and, after receiving initiation, began helping with arrangements at the ashram.
Police are examining the forensic findings, the grinder recovered from the room and other evidence to establish the circumstances leading to Lodhiâs death.

“I have a big decision to make. Will a deal be made with Iran that lets them rebuild and create a far greater country than it ever was before? Or do I annihilate the Islamic Republic? Do I drive them into hell with no chance of survival and no hope of future greatness?” U.S. President Donald Trumpsaid in his UN General Assembly address on September 22. “I believe we’ll make a deal right after the [midterm] election because it doesn’t make sense for them not to,” he added. In the speech, in which Mr. Trump vigorously defended his performance as the President of the U.S., there were 10 references to Iran’s nuclear programme, which he claimed the U.S. had obliterated after its June 2025 bombing. “I will never allow Iran to have a nuclear weapon,” he said. Iran has an advanced nuclear programme but has repeatedly said that it was not seeking to build nuclear weapons.
Mr. Trump’s speech signalled a change in the approach of the administration towards the Iran conflict. In June, when the U.S. signed a memorandum of understanding (MoU) with Iran, Washington agreed to make concessions in return for reopening the Strait of Hormuz, while the nuclear talks were pushed to the back burner. But now, as the stalemate continues, the U.S. seeks to bring the nuclear file back into the negotiations.
Seven-point deal
Iran’s President Masoud Pezeshkian and Foreign Minister Abbas Araghchi were also in New York to attend the UNGA. On the sidelines of the assembly, Mr. Araghchi held indirect talks with U.S. officials, seeking to find a way out of the current impasse. Tehran submitted a seven-point proposal to reopen the Strait of Hormuz in return for the U.S. lifting its naval blockade on Iranian ports, issuing sanctions waivers and releasing Iran’s frozen funds. In effect, Iran wants the U.S. to return to the June 17 MoU. While Iran’s demands remained unchanged, it offered to fast-track the timeline. If the MoU had promised to reopen the Strait of Hormuz in 30 days, Iran now promises to reopen the waterway, which it blockaded in the initial days of the war, in seven days. But Mr. Trump said he rejected the Iranian offer.
Iran, according to Omani Foreign Minister Badr bin Hamad, was ready to make concessions on its nuclear programme on February 27 to avoid war. But Mr. Trump and Israeli Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu chose not to take the deal and started bombing Iran on February 28, killing its Supreme Leader, Ayatollah Ali Khamenei. The war appears to have hardened Iran’s position on the nuclear question.
The blockade of the Strait of Hormuz, through which one-fifth of the world’s oil and gas moved before the war, provided additional leverage to Tehran. Iran sought to tie the reopening of the strait to concessions from the U.S., while keeping its trump card, the nuclear file, close to its chest. The U.S. toed this line when it signed the MoU, which was largely seen as favourable to Iran. But after the collapse of the MoU, the U.S. has been trying to rebuild its lost leverage by easing Iran’s grip on the strait and adding more pain on Iran through economic squeezing.
The Hormuz dilemma
The U.S. attempts to open a safer route along the Omani coast to help tankers get in and out of the Strait of Hormuz have been relatively successful. Whether with Iran’s tolerance or not, shipments through the waterway rose to almost 80% of its prewar levels in September. Before the war, the Gulf region exported nearly 19 million barrels of oil a day through the strait, which fell to a trickle in the first phase of the war, pumping up oil prices. Shipments rose to almost 13 million barrels a day in September, according to ship tracker Huax.
While Arab countries, including Iraq, Saudi Arabia and the UAE manage to sell their crude oil out of the strait, Iran’s oil exports collapsed as it faces the American blockade in the Gulf of Oman. items.title: Trump ‘surprised’ U.K. air base terror suspects out on bail
items.summary: “I’m surprised that they released them,” Mr. Trump told reporters, even as he praised the U.K. authorities for working “very closely” with the U.S.
items.body_text:
U.S. President Donald Trump has said that he was “surprised” that the suspects arrested in connection with an alleged plot at U.K. air base RAF Fairford, in Gloucestershire, were released on bail on Monday (September 28, 2026).
Five British nationals, all men in their twenties, were arrested on Sunday (September 27, 2026) after Gloucestershire police received a call at 4 a.m. on Sunday morning, about three suspicious vehicles near the base, which is used by U.S. forces to conduct strikes on Iran.
“I’m surprised that they released them,” Mr. Trump told reporters, even as he praised the U.K. authorities for working “very closely” with the U.S.
“We know everything about them; we would not have released them,” he added.
Asked if the incident was connected to Iran, Mr. Trump said it “might be”, later saying he knows the answer (to who is involved) but would rather not say.
A foreign actor was “ clearly involved” in the incident, U.S. Secretary of State Marco Rubio said.
The Iranian Embassy in London “categorically” rejected the notion that it was planning an attack on the airbase.
The men, who were arrested first under the Explosives Act and then under the Terrorism Act, still continue to be suspects, Lawrence Taylor, head of U.K. Counterterrorism Policing said.
The suspects, who are all in their twe were released subject to conditions on their movement and contacts with others, he added. According to Mr Taylor, the police were also considering the possibility that the activity might have been undertaken by “proxies”, acting knowingly or unknowingly on behalf of a foreign state.
Deputy Leader of Labour, Lucy Powell pushed back against comments from across the Atlantic, saying on Tuesday (September 29, 2026) that she trusted the police regarding decisions on bail. In the U.K., suspects can be released on ‘police bail’ before they are charged.
Residents of Whelford village which was evacuated on Sunday morning were told they could return home on Monday.

items.title: Spain aims to ban evictions until 2030 amid housing protests
items.summary: Unaffordable housing has been a running sore for years in Spain, but the outcry over last Wednesday's eviction of 87-year-old Madrid pensioner Maricarmen Abascal sparked national uproar.
items.body_text:
The Spanish government on Tuesday (September 29, 2026) approved measures including a ban on evictions until 2030 and the automatic renewal of tenant contracts, a Minister said, following days of nationwide housing protests.
Unaffordable housing has been a running sore for years in Spain, but the outcry over last Wednesday's eviction of 87-year-old Madrid pensioner Maricarmen Abascal sparked national uproar.
Demonstrators have set up around 100 tents in Madrid's emblematic Puerta del Sol square since Saturday night, while tens of thousands of people have protested across the country.
The Socialist-led government raced to finalise a deal with far-left coalition partners Sumar at a key cabinet meeting on Tuesday.
But the measures hang in the balance as the coalition lacks a majority in a heavily fragmented parliament, which must pass them.
Health Minister Monica Garcia listed on social media a series of measures including the eviction ban and the automatic contract renewals, saying what had been achieved was "unimaginable a month ago".
Garcia also mentioned the regulation of short-term rentals and a "ban on the purchase of housing by vulture funds", without providing further details.
"Thank you to the mobilisations and the camps. Without you, this would not have been possible," said the Sumar minister.
Justice Minister Felix Bolanos wrote on X: "Today is a great day for tenants and small homeowners. And a bad one for speculators."
Socialist Housing Minister Isabel Rodriguez was due to offer a press conference with details on the measures agreed by cabinet.
'Structural changes' needed
The camping protesters in central Madrid had warned their movement would continue if the government failed to meet their demands.
Guillermo Mendez, who had travelled hundreds of kilometres from the northern region of Asturias to join the camp, said only "structural changes will change things".
"It has to be something on a national scale, general strikes, protests," the 40-year-old tourist guide told AFP from his green tent.
Abascal, who was evicted on a stretcher from her Madrid home of 70 years, has become a symbol of popular anger at runaway housing prices and a lack of tenant protections.
A deal was announced on Monday for her to return after negotiations with the real estate firm that owned her apartment, which the Madrid Tenants' Union said hiked her monthly rent by 275 percent to 2,650 euros ($3,000).
Mendez said it was "great" Abascal's case had been resolved, but added: "it's a plaster on a huge wound that the economy and society of this country are suffering."

शुरुआती रिपोर्ट के अनुसार हमला नेशनल सोशलिस्ट काउंसिल ऑफ नागालैंड का (युंग आंग गुट) के उग्रवादियों ने किया है। गश्त के दौरान गोलीबारी में हवलदार जानखोकाई कुकी (42) शहीद हो गए। हमला नामपोंग नाले के पास हुआ। इस इलाके में सीमा पर बाड़ लगाने का काम चल रहा है।
हमला NSCN-K-YA गुट ने किया
शुरुआती जांच और खुफिया रिपोर्टों से पता चलता है कि घात लगाकर किए गए हमले के लिए NSCN-K-YA (नेशनल सोशलिस्ट काउंसिल ऑफ नागालैंड का युंग आंग गुट) के उग्रवादी जिम्मेदार हैं।
हमले के बाद, भारतीय सेना और जिला पुलिस ने तुरंत इलाके की घेराबंदी की और भाग रहे उग्रवादियों को पकड़ने के लिए आस-पास के जंगलों में बड़े पैमाने पर तलाशी अभियान शुरू किया।
सुरक्षा बलों ने इलाके में सर्च अभियान तेज किया
पूर्वोत्तर सीमा पर तैनात सीमा सुरक्षा एजेंसियों को हाई अलर्ट पर रखा गया है।अधिकारी ने कहा कि घटना के बाद सुरक्षा बलों ने इलाके में सर्च अभियान तेज कर दिया है।
चांगलांग के एसपी किर्ली पाडु ने कहा कि उन्हें घटना के बारे में जानकारी मिली है और उन्होंने चांगलांग पुलिस स्टेशन के प्रभारी अधिकारी को विवरण इकट्ठा करने का निर्देश दिया है।
चांगलांग जिले में भारत-म्यांमार सीमा क्षेत्र में और अंतरराष्ट्रीय सीमा के पार सक्रिय विद्रोही समूहों की आवाजाही के कारण संवेदनशील बनी हुई है।
-------------------------

items.body_text:
- Hindi News
- National
- Supreme Court Questions Govt On Drug MRP Price Control | India News
कैंसर दवाओं की कीमत पर सुप्रीम कोर्ट बोला- यह नरसंहार:₹2700 की दवा पर कीमत ₹27 हजार कैसे; देश में हर साल ₹5,381 करोड़ का दवा कारोबार
- कॉपी लिंक
सुप्रीम कोर्ट ने मंगलवार को दवाओं की कीमतों पर नाराजगी जताते हुए सवाल किया कि दवाओं के लिए अलग-अलग नियम क्यों हैं। इन पर अधिकतम 16% मार्जिन की सीमा क्यों नहीं तय की जा सकती।
कोर्ट ने कैंसर की एक दवा का उदाहरण दिया, जिसकी रिटेल कीमत करीब ₹2,700 थी, लेकिन MRP ₹27 हजार थी। कोर्ट ने कहा- यह नरसंहार है।
जस्टिस विक्रम नाथ और जस्टिस संदीप मेहता की बेंच ने दवाओं की कीमत, जेनेरिक दवाओं की प्रिस्क्रिप्शन और मेडिकल डिवाइस के कंट्रोल से जुड़ी याचिकाओं पर सुनवाई की।
सरकार के फार्मास्यूटिकल्स विभाग की 2025-26 की वार्षिक रिपोर्ट के मुताबिक, 2024-25 में भारत में कैंसर-रोधी दवाओं की सालाना बिक्री ₹5,281 करोड़ रही। 2021-22 में यह ₹3,382 करोड़ थी। यानी तीन साल में बिक्री करीब 56% बढ़ी। इस कैटेगरी की बिक्री 2021-22 से 2024-25 के बीच 16.01% सालाना की दर से बढ़ी।
कोर्ट रूम LIVE
- सुप्रीम कोर्ट: यदि मरीज सरकारी योजना में इलाज करा रहा है तो इतनी बढ़ी कीमत का भुगतान कौन करता है। इसका बोझ सरकारी खजाने और टैक्सपेयर्स पर ही पड़ता है।
- सॉलिसिटर जनरल तुषार मेहता: यह गंभीर मुद्दा है। ऐसा समाधान जरूरी है, जिसमें मरीजों, सरकार और फार्मा कंपनियों सभी के हितों का संतुलन रहे।
- मेहता: फार्मा कंपनियां लाभ कमाने वाली नहीं हैं। ऐसा लगता है कि लाभ कमाने वाले निजी अस्पताल हैं।
- सुप्रीम कोर्ट: प्राइवेट हॉस्पिटल इंडस्ट्री की तरह काम कर रहे हैं। वे मरीजों को अपनी फार्मेसी से ही दवा खरीदने के लिए मजबूर करते हैं।
- याचिकाकर्ता: जिन दवाओं की कीमत सरकार तय करती है, उनका बाजार में हिस्सा कम है। वहीं, जिनकी कीमत सरकार की तरफ से तय नहीं की गई है, उनका बाजार में करीब 80% या उससे ज्यादा हिस्सा है। उनकी शुरुआती MRP तय करने में कंपनियों को ज्यादा छूट मिलती है।
याचिकाकर्ताओं का कहना है कि इससे दवाओं की कीमत और मरीजों के इलाज का खर्च बढ़ सकता है। कई मरीज इलाज के लिए अपनी संपत्ति या गहने तक बेचने को मजबूर होते हैं।
DPCO 2013 के तहत दवा की कीमत तय करने की प्रक्रिया
ड्रग प्राइस कंट्रोल ऑर्डर (DPCO) का मकसद जरूरी दवाओं की कीमत नियंत्रित रखना है, ताकि कंपनियां मनमानी कीमत न वसूल सकें।
DPCO 2013 के तहत नेशनल लिस्ट ऑफ एसेंशियल मेडिसिन्स (NLEM) में शामिल जरूरी दवाओं की अधिकतम कीमत सरकार तय करती है। इसके लिए बाजार में बिक रही दवाओं की औसत कीमत के आधार पर सीलिंग प्राइस (अधिकतम सीमा) तय की जाती है। इस कीमत से ज्यादा पर दवा बेचना गैरकानूनी है।
स्वास्थ्य मंत्रालय की विशेषज्ञ समिति दवाओं की सुरक्षा, असर और कीमत को देखते हुए जरूरी दवाओं का चयन करती है। इसमें देश में आम बीमारियों और लोगों की स्वास्थ्य जरूरतों का भी ध्यान रखा जाता है।
इस लिस्ट की समय-समय पर समीक्षा की जाती है और जरूरत के अनुसार नई दवाएं जोड़ी जाती हैं। जो दवाएं इस सूची में नहीं होतीं, उनकी कीमतों पर सरकार का सीधा नियंत्रण कम होता है।
नोट- यहां गैर-आवश्यक का मतलब बेकार दवा नहीं है, बल्कि ऐसी दवा है जो NLEM में शामिल नहीं है।
------------------------------
ये खबर भी पढ़ें…
ज्यादा गर्म चाय का शौक खतरनाक, 65°C से ज्यादा गर्म तो कैंसर का रिस्क, चाय, कॉफी, सूप हमेशा ठंडा करके पिएं
आपने अक्सर लोगों को यह कहते हुए सुना होगा। हमारे यहां अच्छी चाय की पहचान सिर्फ उसके स्वाद से नहीं, उसकी गर्माहट से भी होती है। मेहमान के सामने चाय रख दी जाए और वह थोड़ी ठंडी निकल जाए, तो कई लोग इसे मेजबानी की कमी मान लेते हैं। लेकिन जिस गर्माहट को हम स्वाद, ताजगी और सुकून से जोड़ते हैं, वही शरीर के लिए परेशानी की वजह भी बन सकती है। पूरी खबर पढ़ें…

items.summary: चुनाव आयोग के पोर्टल ECINet में स्थानीय चुनाव अधिकारियों के अधिकारों को लेकर उठे सवालों के बीच महाराष्ट्र के मुख्य निर्वाचन अधिकारी एस चोकलिंगम का 24 सितंबर को लिखा लेटर मंगलवार को सामने आया। चोकलिंगम ने इसमें वोटर रिकॉर्ड की गड़बड़ियों से जुड़े मामलों में ERO को ज्यादा अधिकार देने और सॉफ्टवेयर में 4 बदलाव की मांग की थी। उनका कहना था कि किसी वोटर के रिकॉर्ड में गड़बड़ी मिलने पर हर मामले में एक जैसी प्रक्रिया लागू नहीं होनी चाहिए। इलेक्टोरल रजिस्ट्रेशन ऑफिसर यानी ERO को यह तय करने का अधिकार होना
items.body_text:
- Hindi News
- National
- Maharashtra ECINet Software Updates | Election Commission Proposal
'SIR में स्थानीय अफसरों को ज्यादा अधिकार मिलें':महाराष्ट्र CEO ने भी लेटर लिखा था, 4 मांगें की थीं; दो चुनाव आयुक्त भी जता चुके आपत्ति
- कॉपी लिंक
चुनाव आयोग के पोर्टल ECINet में स्थानीय चुनाव अधिकारियों के अधिकारों को लेकर उठे सवालों के बीच महाराष्ट्र के मुख्य निर्वाचन अधिकारी एस चोकलिंगम का 24 सितंबर को लिखा लेटर मंगलवार को सामने आया।
चोकलिंगम ने इसमें वोटर रिकॉर्ड की गड़बड़ियों से जुड़े मामलों में ERO को ज्यादा अधिकार देने और सॉफ्टवेयर में 4 बदलाव की मांग की थी।
उनका कहना था कि किसी वोटर के रिकॉर्ड में गड़बड़ी मिलने पर हर मामले में एक जैसी प्रक्रिया लागू नहीं होनी चाहिए। इलेक्टोरल रजिस्ट्रेशन ऑफिसर यानी ERO को यह तय करने का अधिकार होना चाहिए कि किस वोटर को सुनवाई के लिए बुलाना है, कौन से दस्तावेज लेने हैं और किन मामलों को अपने स्तर पर निपटाया जा सकता है।
उनसे पहले चुनाव आयुक्त सुखबीर सिंह संधू और विवेक जोशी भी ECINet में स्थानीय अधिकारियों के अधिकार सीमित करने पर आपत्ति जताने की खबरें आई थीं। एक मीडिया रिपोर्ट में दावा किया गया था कि दोनों ने 10 महीनों में कम से कम 14 बार आयोग के फैसलों पर लिखित आपत्ति जताई थी।
एस चोकलिंगम ने कहा था- हर मामले में सुनवाई की जरूरत न पड़े
महाराष्ट्र CEO ने अपने लेटर में खासतौर पर उन मामलों का जिक्र किया, जिनमें रिकॉर्ड में गड़बड़ी मिलने के बाद मतदाताओं को नोटिस दिया जाता है।
उनका कहना है कि बुजुर्गों, दिव्यांगों और दूसरे कमजोर वर्गों के लोगों को हर मामले में व्यक्तिगत सुनवाई के लिए बुलाने की जरूरत नहीं होनी चाहिए। सॉफ्टवेयर में ERO को मामले के हिसाब से फैसला लेने का विकल्प मिलना चाहिए।
विवाद के बीच 26 सितंबर को दिल्ली में चुनाव आयोग की बैठक हुई। इसमें आपत्तियों पर फैसला लिए गए।
आपत्ति: सुनवाई का फैसला ERO करें: कौन से मामले में मतदाता को बुलाना है, यह ERO तय कर सकें
बदलाव: अब किसी मतदाता, जिसका नाम वोटर लिस्ट में नहीं है या उसके जानकारी में गड़बड़ी है- के मामले में BLO घर जाकर दस्तावेज लेगा। मतदाता को सामान्य तौर पर ERO/AERO के सामने सुनवाई के लिए नहीं बुलाया जाएगा। केवल अपवाद वाले मामलों में ERO तय करेगा कि सुनवाई जरूरी है। सुनवाई संभव हो तो ऑनलाइन होगी।
आपत्ति : दस्तावेज तय करने की छूट। ERO जरूरत के हिसाब से दस्तावेज स्वीकार कर सकें।
बदलाव: आयोग ने कहा कि BLO संबंधित मतदाता से दस्तावेज लेकर ECINet पर अपलोड करेंगे और ERO उन दस्तावेजों के आधार पर फैसला करेगा। आयोग ने अलग से यह स्पष्ट नहीं किया कि ERO को तय लिस्ट से बाहर कोई भी दस्तावेज स्वीकार करने की छूट दे दी गई है।
आपत्ति: मामले खुद निपटा सकें: ERO को कुछ मामलों में अपने स्तर पर फैसला लेने की सुविधा मिले। बदलाव: आयोग ने कहा कि फैसला ERO करेगा।
आपत्ति : सॉफ्टवेयर में अधिकार मिलें: ECINet में ERO के कानूनी अधिकारों के मुताबिक विकल्प दिए जाएं। बदलाव: आयोग ने ECINet की समीक्षा के लिए कमेटी बनाई है। समिति की अध्यक्षता सीनियर उप चुनाव आयुक्त करेंगे। इसमें IIT या IIIT के एक्सपर्ट को भी शामिल किया जाएगा। आयोग ने कहा कि फील्ड अधिकारियों को और लचीलापन चाहिए तो सॉफ्टवेयर में उसकी व्यवस्था की जाएगी।
महाराष्ट्र में SIR जारी, ड्राफ्ट लिस्ट में 21% मतदाताओं के नाम कटे
महाराष्ट्र की ड्राफ्ट वोटर लिस्ट 31 अगस्त को जारी हुई थी। ड्राफ्ट में राज्य के करीब 21.1% मतदाताओं की संख्या कम हुई थी। अंतिम वोटर लिस्ट 16 नवंबर को जारी होनी है।
फिलहाल ड्राफ्ट लिस्ट पर दावे और आपत्तियों की प्रक्रिया चल रही है। इसी दौरान रिकॉर्ड में गड़बड़ी वाले मामलों की जांच और नोटिस की प्रक्रिया भी जारी है।
आयोग के फैसलों पर सुप्रीम कोर्ट में अगले हफ्ते सुनवाई
इधर, सुप्रीम कोर्ट ने मंगलवार को चुनाव आयोग के फैसलों पर सवाल उठाने वाली याचिका पर अगले हफ्ते सुनवाई करने की सहमति दी है। याचिका में CEC ज्ञानेश कुमार की अध्यक्षता वाले चुनाव आयोग के फैसलों पर सवाल उठाए गए हैं।
मामला CJI सूर्यकांत, जस्टिस जॉयमाल्या बागची और जस्टिस वी. मोहना की बेंच के सामने रखा गया। सीनियर वकील विकास सिंह ने कहा कि चुनाव आयोग के फैसले कानून के मुताबिक सर्वसम्मति या बहुमत से होने चाहिए।
23 सितंबर: EC के अंदर मतभेद की रिपोर्ट सामने आई
चोकलिंगम के लेटर से एक दिन पहले, 23 सितंबर को इंडियन एक्सप्रेस ने चुनाव आयोग के अंदर मतभेद से जुड़ी एक रिपोर्ट आई थी। रिपोर्ट के मुताबिक, चुनाव आयुक्त सुखबीर सिंह संधू और विवेक जोशी ने 10 महीनों में कम से कम 14 बार आयोग के फैसलों पर लिखित आपत्ति जताई थी।

items.title: India break athletics gold jinx with women's 4x400m relay win
items.summary: India break athletics gold jinx with womens xm relay win
items.body_text:
India break athletics gold jinx in Asian Games 2026 with women's 4x400m relay win
India finally clinched its first athletics gold of the Asian Games 2026, with the women's 4x400m relay team triumphing in the final. Vithya Ramraj, Kiran Pahal, Machettira Poovamma and Prachi held their nerve to deliver a memorable victory for India.
India finally broke their athletics gold jinx at the Asian Games 2026, doing so in spectacular fashion as the women’s 4x400m relay team of Vithya Ramraj, Kiran Pahal, Machettira Poovamma and Prachi stormed to gold in Aichi-Nagoya on Tuesday, September 29.
The Indian quartet clocked 3:29.69 to finish ahead of Bahrain, who claimed silver in 3:30.21, while China took bronze in 3:31.02. The victory gave India their first athletics gold of the Games after a string of silver and bronze medals.
Kiran Pahal opened the race and handed over in third. Poovamma then produced a strong second leg to move India into the lead, before Prachi kept the team ahead. Ramraj took the baton for the anchor leg and held off Bahrain’s Salwa Eid Nasr in the closing stages to seal gold for India.
Asian Games, September 29 Updates
India were in danger of finishing an Asian Games campaign without an athletics gold for the first time since the 1994 Hiroshima Games. However, the women’s relay team came through in emphatic fashion to ensure India would not leave the Asiad without the top prize in athletics.
VITHYA RAMRAJ COMPLETES MEMORABLE MEDAL HAUL
The gold capped a memorable campaign for Vithya Ramraj, who claimed her third medal of the Games. She had earlier won silver in the mixed 4x400m relay before securing bronze in the women’s 400m hurdles.
In the 400m hurdles final, Vithya clocked 54.75 seconds to finish third. She finished behind UAE’s Mariam Kareem, who won gold in 54.31 seconds, and Kazakhstan’s Adelina Zems, who took silver in 54.58 seconds. India’s Anu Raghavan finished fifth.
Vithya returned to the track on Tuesday and played a key role in India’s gold-medal-winning relay quartet. The victory completed a remarkable three-medal haul for the athlete at Aichi-Nagoya.
Her bronze in the 400m hurdles was particularly significant, with her 54.75 seconds eclipsing PT Usha’s national record of 55.42 seconds, which had stood for 42 years. She then added another silver as part of the mixed 4x400m relay team before finishing her campaign with gold.
HOW INDIA'S DAY IN ATHLETICS WENT
India’s athletics campaign on Tuesday had already produced medals before the women’s 4x400m relay took centre stage. Pooja won bronze in the women’s high jump, while Gulveer Singh added bronze in the men’s 5000m with a time of 13:32.75.
Gulveer completed a hat-trick of medals after earlier winning silver in the 10,000m and 1500m. India also secured bronze in the mixed 4x100m relay.
India signed off in style with another bronze in the men’s 4x400m relay. Dharmveer Choudhary, Manu Thekkinalil, Jay Kumar and Vishal Thennarasu clocked 3:01.61, finishing behind Japan (3:00.75) and Qatar (3:00.93) in a thrilling final.
There were disappointments too, with Avinash Sable not starting the men’s 5000m final after missing the podium in the 3000m steeplechase. In the women’s hammer throw, Tanya Chaudhary finished fourth with a personal best of 63.35m, while Anushka Yadav was fifth with 64.56m.
But the evening ultimately belonged to India’s women’s 4x400m relay team. Their performance sealed gold, ending India’s wait for an athletics gold at the 2026 Asian Games.

items.title: PS5, iPhones, Prada perfumes looted from LPU's Uni Mall. But no book thief there
items.summary: PS iPhones Prada perfumes looted from LPUs Uni Mall But no book thief there
items.body_text:
PS5, iPhones, Prada perfumes looted from LPU's Uni Mall, but books go untouched
PS5s, phones, laptops, high-end perfumes and lakhs of cash have been looted from LPU's Uni Mall during the violent protests. While the shops of electronics and daily needs were vandalised, and their counters were emptied, the stores selling books and other stationary items were left untouched. The contrast has become a talking point.
The stocked-up Sony PlayStation 5s were gone. So were mobile phones, laptops, expensive perfumes, and lakhs of rupees in cash. Glass counters were smashed, shelves were emptied and even phones that customers had left for repairs were taken from Lovely Professional University (LPU)'s Uni Mall after a student protest turned violent over the weekend. But, amid the broken glass facades and ransacked stores, something was left untouched. The books.
"They looted all the other shops but left the books," a person at the LPU's Uni mall told The Lallantop, India Today Digital's sister portal. Asked why, the response was, "They left the books because they were of no use to them. Whatever they thought would be useful, they picked up and took away."
Uni Mall, inside LPU's Phagwara campus, was vandalised, and several shops were looted during unrest on the intervening night of September 26 and 27. LPU's Uni Mall is a multi-storey, air-conditioned shopping complex inside the Phagwara campus. It houses shops, eateries, book and stationery stores, electronics outlets and other services for students and staff. Shopkeepers told The Lallantop that PS5s, phones, laptops, expensive perfumes, electronic accessories and cash were among the things taken, with some estimating their losses in tens of lakhs.
Videos of the looting have also gone viral on social media, showing people with their faces covered with bandannas ransacking shops and carrying away goods. LPU students have claimed that those involved were outsiders. However, some videos that have surfaced also appear to show people claiming that students were among those involved in the looting. "Free ki shopping chal rahi hai bhai," a man says in one of the videos narrating what was happening.
Books, however, were left untouched even as stores around them were ransacked.
New Delhi-based history coach and author Siddharth's Echelon, took to X to share a few videos of the looting and said, "Ironically, no one even touched bookshops. They didn't even tear the posters of those shops."
"Priorities are crystal clear," wrote a person named Taniya Verma, on X.
The LPU on Tuesday put around 30-40 students under the scanner for alleged involvement in the violence and vandalism. The university is examining CCTV footage and other material to identify those responsible. Dean of Student Welfare, Prof Sourabh Lakhanpal also alleged that outsiders were involved, pointing to videos of masked people carrying rods, while saying any wider conspiracy remained a matter for investigation.
HOW THE LPU PROTEST ERUPTED
The violence and vandalism followed protests at the LPU campus after claims of a female student being sexually assaulted began circulating among students and on social media. Students came out of their hostels in large numbers, and the protest later turned violent. Uni Mall was vandalised and traffic was disrupted on the Jalandhar-Phagwara stretch of NH-44.
LPU rejected claims of a sexual assault on campus as "false, baseless and fabricated". Police subsequently registered a case on a complaint and constituted an SIT to investigate the allegations and the violence.
It has not been independently established that everyone involved in the looting was an LPU student. Students have alleged that outsiders were also present during the unrest, and police have been examining CCTV footage to identify those involved.

items.title: Opinion | Praised one day, pictured the next: The Shah-Modi signal to Yogi before 2027 has caught the Opposition flat-footed
items.summary: Know expert political analysis on how PM Modi and Amit Shah's recent public backing of UP CM Yogi Adityanath sends a clear signal to the opposition ahead of the 2027 assembly elections.
items.body_text:
Image Credit: Uttar Pradesh Chief Minister Yogi Adityanath addresses a programme. (IANS/File photo)
- By Dr. Abhay Pandey
In politics, words often start an argument. Pictures often close it. On Saturday, the photograph of Chief Minister Yogi Adityanath's meeting with Prime Minister Narendra Modi in Delhi moved across social media with unusual speed. The Prime Minister's Office shared it. The Chief Minister thanked the Prime Minister and said his guidance gives new energy to the building of a "new Uttar Pradesh." In official language, this was a courtesy meeting. In political language, it is being treated as a plain signal from the Centre ahead of the 2027 Vidhan Sabha elections.
The picture did not arrive in isolation. Only a day earlier, Home Minister Amit Shah had praised Yogi Adityanath in public. Speaking at a trade fair in Greater Noida, Shah said the face of Uttar Pradesh has changed, the mafia has been finished, the rule of law has been put in place, and places once known for the desi katta now make BrahMos missiles and AK-203 rifles. This was not polite praise for the occasion. For months there had been speculation about the organisation, about faces, and about leadership. Shah's words put a stop to that talk. One day the compliment, the next day a photograph with the Prime Minister. The sequence itself is the message.
Uttar Pradesh politics does not forget its photographs. In November 2021, at Lucknow's Raj Bhavan, the Prime Minister's hand rested on Yogi Adityanath's shoulder. The image went viral when the election was already at the door. The opposition made fun of it. The BJP read it as full support. Defence Minister Rajnath Singh later said the Prime Minister had told Yogi he was playing like a sharp, attacking batsman and should keep his form. In February 2022, just before voting, another photograph appeared – both leaders with their hands raised. That was not a chance. It was planning. Even then, rumours said all was not well between Delhi and Lucknow. The picture pushed those rumours to the side.
The same mind game is being played again. The election is still some way off, but the organisation has already started work. Talk of booths, of western Uttar Pradesh, and of internal stock-taking has been in the air for some time. At such a moment, a stamp from the Centre calms the worker and unsettles the opposition. For the Samajwadi Party and other parties, one part of the plan has been to assume that the ruling camp is pulling in different directions. When a rift is visible, the attack is easy. When unity is visible, the attack loses its bite.
Elections are not fought only with manifestos. They are also fought with signs. A hand on the shoulder, or a meeting photograph issued from an official account, does the same job: it removes doubt. The worker wants to know on whose face the fight will be fought. When that answer comes from the Centre, confidence rises, discipline improves, and inner rivalry is pushed down. The opposition wants to know where the split is. When the answer comes back that there is no split, its story begins to fall apart.
This is not to say that one photograph decides an election. Even in 2022, the win did not come from a picture alone. Law and order, welfare schemes, the organisation, and a scattered opposition strategy all moved together. But the photograph set the mood. In an election, mood arrives before the numbers. It pulls the worker to the booth and forces the other side onto the back foot.
That is why the opposition's restlessness is only natural. It would like the debate to stay on Yogi versus Yogi or Centre versus the state. If the Centre is seen standing with the state’s main face, the debate returns to development, crime, and governance. That has not been comfortable ground for the opposition. Calling the photograph "ordinary courtesy" therefore suits it. The public, however, does not treat such signs as ordinary.
The value of a message sent before an election should not be counted

items.title: Two MHA officials arrested by Delhi Police Special Cell over FCRA registration bribery scandal
items.summary: Delhi Police Special Cell arrested two Ministry of Home Affairs accounts officials for allegedly demanding bribes to fast-track FCRA registration approvals.
items.body_text:
Two officials working in accounts of the Ministry of Home Affairs have been apprehended by the Special Cell of the Delhi Police, based on actionable intelligence provided by the Ministry of Home Affairs, in relation to bribery demands for speedy registration under the Foreign Contribution Regulation Act.
Arrest and function of the arrested officials
Federal and local law enforcement authorities arrested the two officials of the MHA in New Delhi during a sting operation on September 28. The first suspect belongs to the Foreigners Division of the MHA, whereas the second one works in the Pay and Accounts Office after having served his tenure in the Foreigners Division of the MHA.
Based on the initial investigation reports of the Ministry, it is found that both the officials made contact with the troubled association and demanded illegal money in return for processing of their registration documents. It is being investigated whether there was a syndicate of the two officials and whether they had processed approvals and renewals for many associations using such means.
MHA reiterates its policy of zero tolerance and online service
Home Ministry made a strict warning after the arrests, stating the ministry’s zero tolerance for corruption and clarifying that stringent criminal and departmental steps are being taken. The officials stressed that all the applications, submissions, and renewals under FCRA are processed solely through the online digital portal.
None of the third-party agents or brokers is authorised to help in processing or speeding up any kind of FCRA services. This is because the system, regulated through the Foreign Contribution Regulation Act of 2010, manages the flow of foreign money to Indian NGOs, firms, and organizations.

items.title: Sambhal violence: Supreme Court sets aside high court order, imposes Rs 10 lakh cost on UP administration
items.summary: Know how the Supreme Court quashed the NSA detention of Sambhal violence accused Mulla Afroz, penalizing the UP government with a ₹10 lakh fine over custody confessions.
items.body_text:
The Supreme Court has imposed a ₹10 lakh fine on the Uttar Pradesh Government, holding that any preventive detention cannot be based on alleged confessions obtained in police custody. Justice Dipankar Datta and Sheel Nagu pronounced the judgment while rejecting an appeal filed by Mulla Afroz, who is accused in the Sambhal Violence Case of 2024.
Challenge to police custody confessions and NSA provision
Mulla Afroz was arrested under Section 3(2) of the National Security Act (NSA) in October 2025 due to the violent clash during the Sambhal Shahi Jama Masjid Survey, where four people were killed. The Uttar Pradesh state officials justified the preventive arrest on grounds that his acts posed a threat to public order and hence required stringent measures to be taken to maintain peace.
The Supreme Court raised doubt over the legality of the very justification being provided by the state in relation to the invocation of preventive detention on grounds of statements given by a person in police custody. Afroz filed a special leave petition challenging the rejection of his bail petition filed in June 2026 by the Allahabad High Court in support of the subjectivity of the District Magistrate in making such orders.
Verdict follows reserved judgment
The apex court concluded proceedings and reserved its judgment on September 8 before issuing the final ruling and financial penalty against the state administration. The ruling sets a strict legal precedent regarding the limits of preventive detention and the inadmissibility of custody-based confessions for restricting personal liberty.

items.title: NHRC directs Etah Police to register FIR, Meta to respond after complaint against ‘home tutor’ Pratibha, who was brainwashing children with anti-Modi hate: Details
items.summary: After OpIndia reported about a home tutor Pratibha using her Instagram page with a misleading bio and posting videos featuring school children hurling abuses at PM Modi, the National Human Rights Commission (NHRC) has initiated action.
items.body_text:
On 28th September, the National Human Rights Commission took cognisance of a complaint filed by the Sewa Nyaya Uthhan Foundation against exploitation of minor children for creation and circulation of abusive and derogatory content on Instagram by a purported coaching centre with account name “Pratibha_ed_squad”. The coaching centre publishing politically charged videos using children, operates from Uttar Pradesh’s Etah district.
The complaint alleges that children are being scripted, tutored, and frequently made to appear in videos containing abusive, derogatory, and politically charged expressions. The videos are recorded and uploaded on the Instagram handle “Pratibha_edu_squad” for reach and engagement.
“It is alleged that children, including those belonging to socially and economically vulnerable backgrounds, are being scripted, tutored, and repeatedly made to appear in videos containing abusive, derogatory, and politically charged expressions, which are thereafter uploaded and circulated publicly for digital reach and engagement. The complaint further alleges that a large number of such videos depicting minor children have been uploaded on the platform, raising serious concerns regarding their dignity, privacy, psychological well-being, informed parental consent and possible exploitation by adults controlling or facilitating such content,” the NHRC notice states.
“The allegations, if established, disclose serious issues concerning the care, protection and dignity of children and their alleged use by adults for creation, publication and amplification of digital content, warranting examination under the human-rights jurisdiction of the Commission,” it adds.
The NHRC Bench headed by Member Priyank Kanoongo has issued notices to the Etah Senior Superintendent of Police, District Magistrate, Meta India’s Managing Director and Country Head, in addition to the Secretary of the Ministry of Electronics and Information Technology (MeitY).
The Commission has directed Etah Police to identify the children seen in the derogatory videos uploaded by ‘Pratibha_ed_squad’ and ensure that they are provided appropriate protection and counselling.
“Identify the children appearing in the impugned videos and ensure that they are produced before the competent Child Welfare Committee (CWC), wherever warranted, for assessment of their care, protection, safety and well-being. Necessary counselling/psychosocial support shall be provided through the CWC/DCPU, while strictly protecting the identity and privacy of the children,” the notice reads.
In addition, the police have been directed to identify the individuals running the social media in question and probe the role of adults involved in scripting, recording, uploading, or otherwise facilitating the content.
“Ascertain the identity of the person(s) operating or controlling the social-media handle. recording or creating the videos, scripting or prompting the children, uploading, circulating the content and otherwise facilitating or benefiting from such activity, including the role, if any, of parents/guardians, tuition/coaching operators or other adults,” the notice adds.
Furthermore, the NHRC has directed the police to examine the digital material in question, identify commission of cognisable offence, and register FIR against those involved in creating, recording, uploading, circulation, or facilitation of such concent as well as the concerned social media platform Meta/Instagram.
“Examine the entire digital material and, where commission of any cognizable offence is disclosed, ensure registration of FIR and investigation against all persons/entities responsibly, including the person(s) creating, recording, uploading, circulating or facilitating such content and the concerned social-media platform/intermediary, wherever its role or liability is disclosed, under the applicable provisions of the Juvenile Justice (Care and Protcction of Children) Act, 2015, Bharatiya Nyaya Sanhita, 2023, 1nformation T

items.title: Violent protests rock LPU: Read the story behind the ‘Lovely’ in Lovely Professional University
items.summary: From a ₹500 loan and a small sweet shop in Jalandhar to a ₹2,000-crore education empire, this is the story behind the ‘Lovely’ in Lovely Professional University
items.body_text:
Lovely Professional University (LPU) is under the spotlight due to protests over the rape of a girl on campus. What began as a protest over the incident soon turned violent, with students clashing with police, damaging property and blocking the Jalandhar-Phagwara National Highway.
Protest turns violent at LPU
The protest began late on Saturday, September 26, near the girls’ hostel after information about a sexual assault involving a female student started circulating among students. By around 2 am, students from different hostels had gathered and moved towards the university’s main gate. Videos from inside the campus, including the university mall and other areas, showed agitated students protesting against the sexual assault.
The situation escalated on Sunday, September 27, when protesters damaged property, pelted stones at police and set vehicles on fire. Four to five police vehicles were damaged, while at least two vehicles were set on fire, according to police. Several police personnel were injured in the clashes.
Students later blocked NH-44 outside the university from around 4 am, leading to major traffic disruption. Police said the situation became tense when officers tried to clear the highway blockade, and some protesters threw water bottles at them. Police then used a lathi charge, after which the students moved back towards the campus.
In the aftermath, LPU suspended classes for 10 days from September 28 and postponed the midterm examinations until further notice.
But as LPU finds itself in the headlines, the institution’s history offers another story, one that begins not in education, but with a small sweet shop in Jalandhar.
LPU came into existence in 2005
The Lovely Professional University came into existence in 2005, when the Lovely Professional University Act, 2005, was passed by the Punjab State Legislature. The Act received the Governor’s assent on December 23, 2005. The university started its first academic session in 2006, after receiving recognition from the University Grants Commission (UGC).
But even before the university was established, the name “Lovely” had already become a familiar name in Punjab. The name came from the business started by the Mittal family decades earlier.
How the ‘Lovely’ name began
The story of Lovely goes back to 1961, when Baldev Raj Mittal opened a small sweet shop in Jalandhar Cantt. He named it “Lovely Sweets.” Baldev, who was originally from Rajasthan, had earlier helped his father run a canteen for soldiers in Sialkot. After Partition, the battalion moved to Ferozepur.
With a Rs 500 loan from the battalion’s commanding officer, Baldev started the sweet shop in Sadar Bazaar, Jalandhar Cantt. The shop became known for its sweets, especially because of its focus on purity and taste. The family later expanded the business and opened another shop and a manufacturing centre in Jalandhar city in 1986.
Baldev’s sons Ramesh Mittal and Naresh Mittal joined the family business and continued the sweets trade. The family followed a high-volume, low-margin business model, selling products such as laddoos and pedas.
From sweets to automobiles and education
The youngest son, Ashok Kumar Mittal, later took the family business into automobiles. In 1991, he secured a Bajaj dealership through Lovely Autos, followed by a Maruti dealership around 1996.
By the late 1990s, the family had entered the private education sector. They started an engineering college in 2000, after earlier efforts to get AICTE approval for a management college faced a delay of two years. The family’s background in the sweets business was also discussed during that period.
The Lovely name continued with each new business. When the Punjab legislature passed the university law in 2005, the family carried the same name into higher education, leading to the establishment of Lovely Professional University.

items.body_text:
The Somnath Temple in Gujarat has been a symbol of devotion, resistance, and civilisational continuity. The holy abode of Someshwara Mahadev has been witness to around 18 Islamic jihadist attacks. While historical records document and folklore glorify how the temple priests and local devotees fought against Mahmud Ghazni’s Jihadis, Islamo-leftists today discredit their resistance using imaginary claims. In this vein, leftist propagandist Mrinal Pande recently claimed that the priests of Somnath Temple sat outside singing Bhajans when Islamic armies from Ghazni plundered the temple.
In an X post published on 25th September, Mrinal Pande wrote, “When the Somnath temple was being looted by the armies from Ghazni, the priests sat singing Bhajans outside the temple, asking for god’s blessings.”
Pande drew equivalence between the myth of Roman Emperor Nero playing a flute while Rome burned, and the Islamo-leftists-concocted lie that Somnath Temple priests were singing Bhajans instead of fighting back when Mahmud Ghazni campaigned against the Hindu temple.
Before delving into the truth of whether Somnath Temple priests actually just sat outside and sang Bhajans or posed a strong fight against Jihadi invaders, let us revisit the history of Somnath Temple and its destruction.
The Somnath Mandir is a majestic temple situated near Prabhas Patan of Veraval in Gujarat. It is one of Lord Shiva’s twelve sacred Jyotirlingas and is mentioned in Chapter 13 of the Shiv Purana. Somnath is also described as Triveni Sangam, much like the one in Prayagraj, due to the meeting of the Kapila, Hiran, and Saraswati rivers.
For Muslims, especially the Islamic invaders in the medieval era, destroying the temples and idols of the Kafirs was upheld as their “religious duty,” and despite changes in times, this Islamist desire has not subsided. Although numerous Hindu temples were desecrated and destroyed during the Islamic invasions, Somnath in Gujarat and Jagannath Temple in Puri, Odisha, faced the maximum attacks, with each being invaded 17 and 18 times.
The first attack on the Somnath Temple came in 725 CE from an Arab named Junayd ibn Abd ar-Rahman al-Murri, also known as Al-Junayd during the Umayyad Caliphate. Junayd was appointed the governor of Sindh in 723. He invaded Gujarat and Rajasthan and ravaged, looted, and destroyed the Somnath Mandir in 725.
It was only in 815 CE that Nagabhata II, a Gurjar Pratihar monarch, visited the ruins of the Somnath Temple and rebuilt the temple using red stones.
The next major attack on the Somnath Temple was in 1025 by Mahmud of Ghazni, who went on to lead 17 invasions of Hindu temples.
In 1025, he plundered the holy idol of Somnath during his sixteenth expedition to India. “Somnath” is Sanskrit for “moon master.” Mahmud of Ghazni is said to have sworn to wage an annual Jihad against the country of Kafirs. Ghazni overthrew Hindu king Jayapala, defeated his successors Anandpala (in 1008) and Trilochanpala (in 1013).
In 1011, Mahmud of Ghazni attacked Thaneshwar and destroyed idols. He burned the temples in Mathura during 1018–1019, and the idols were taken to Ghazni. His Jihadi fanaticism also devoured Mathura, Kannauj, and the many temples on the way. However, Ghazni’s Somnath invasion became an unforgettable chapter in Bharat’s history, reflecting both the obsession and abhorrence Muslims harbour for Hindus, and the resilience of the Hindu civilisation to rise every time and continue the fight until the ultimate victory, no matter how long it takes.
Despite enduring heavy losses and fierce opposition, the Jihadi army of Mahmud of Ghazni demolished the sacred temple.
Defenceless guardians of the Somnath Temple fought till the end of their lives

items.summary: The announcement, which Trump made on his social media platform, buys time for more negotiations and avoids, for now, another strain in already tense relations between the historic allies.
items.body_text:
Trump Says US and Canada Have Reached Last-Minute Deal to Delay 50% US Tariffs on Canadian Imports
The announcement, which Trump made on his social media platform, buys time for more negotiations and avoids, for now, another strain in already tense relations between the historic allies.
- World News
- 4 min read
Washington: President Donald Trump said Tuesday he was delaying 50% U.S. tariffs on $20 billion worth of Canadian imports after the two countries reached a last-minute deal hours before the sanctions were to go into effect.
The announcement, which Trump made on his social media platform, buys time for more negotiations and avoids, for now, another strain in already tense relations between the historic allies.
“I have paused the 50% Tariffs against Canada, that were scheduled to kick in tomorrow morning for three days, based on the fact that Canada and the U.S.A., subject to the finalisation of documents, have a DEAL!” Trump posted on Truth Social less than two hours before the 12:01 a.m. Wednesday deadline.
If they had gone into effect as scheduled at 12:01 a.m. Wednesday, Trump’s import taxes would have hit Canadian products ranging from hockey sticks to tongue depressors.
Advertisement
But the political impact would likely have been bigger than the economic one. Canada had threatened to retaliate against any new tariffs with levies of its own, aggravating a trade fight between countries that sold each other $880 billion worth of goods and services last year.
Canadian officials did not immediately respond to requests for comment Tuesday night.
Advertisement
Canadian Prime Minister Mark Carney and Trump had spoken twice by phone in the past two days about the ongoing negotiations, including a call Tuesday afternoon, Carney’s office said, underscoring the last-minute push for a deal.
Both countries had reason to step back from the brink. Nearly 72% of Canada’s goods exports last year went to the United States. And the Trump administration would be taking a risk by imposing a hefty new tariff — paid by U.S. importers who try to pass along the cost to consumers via higher prices — ahead of November’s midterm elections. U.S. voters are already frustrated with the high cost of living.
“I don’t think either side really wants these tariffs to come into effect,’’ Ryan Majerus, a partner at King & Spalding and a former U.S. trade official, said before the delay was announced. “There’s a pretty strong push on both sides to find an off-ramp here.’’
Trump’s approach to dealing with Canada marks an extraordinary departure from the traditionally cooperative relationship between the two countries. Trump has hit Canadian goods with tariffs — in a push to bring manufacturing back to the U.S. — and has repeatedly made inflammatory comments about turning Canada into America’s 51st state.
Trump has made tariffs the centrepiece of his second-term economic agenda. Last year, he imposed double-digit import taxes on almost every country, justifying them by declaring the longstanding U.S. trade deficit a national emergency. The Supreme Court in February ruled that he’d overstepped his authority, striking down those tariffs and setting the stage for the federal government to pay refunds to importers.
So Trump has looked for other legal authority to impose tariffs.
To hit Canada, he reached back to the Great Depression, invoking Section 338 of the Tariff Act of 1930 to threaten 50% tariffs on products that account for about 5% of Canadian exports to the United States.
Nearly a century ago, with the U.S. and world economies in collapse, Congress passed the 1930 tariff law, imposing taxes on imports from around the world. Known as the Smoot-Hawley tariffs, named for their congressional sponsors, they are notorious among economists and historians for limiting world commerce and making the Great Depression worse.
Section 338 tariffs have never been used before.
Section 338 authorises the president to impose tariffs of up to 50% on imports from count

items.title: 'Allegations Lack Seriousness': Turkiye Denies Israel's Claims Over Syria Airstrikes
items.summary: "These air strikes should stop, and we stand against them," Dujarric said at a UN press briefing on Tuesday. As per Al Jazeera, Egypt's Foreign Ministry also condemned the Israeli strikes, calling them a "dangerous escalation that threatens security and stability in the region".
items.body_text:
'Allegations Lack Seriousness': Turkiye Denies Israel's Claims Over Syria Airstrikes
"These air strikes should stop, and we stand against them," Dujarric said at a UN press briefing on Tuesday. As per Al Jazeera, Egypt's Foreign Ministry also condemned the Israeli strikes, calling them a "dangerous escalation that threatens security and stability in the region".
- World News
- 3 min read
Ankara: Turkiye on Wednesday rejected Israel's claim that its airstrikes on Syria's Abu al-Duhur military airport were linked to a planned Turkish troop deployment, saying the allegations "lack seriousness" and seek to legitimise strikes on Syria's sovereignty and territorial integrity.
In a post on X, the Turkish Presidential Communications Directorate said, “The allegations put forward by the Israeli Prime Ministry, which lack seriousness, aim to legitimize Israel's unlawful airstrikes targeting the sovereignty and territorial integrity of Syria.” It added, "The accusations raised stem from Netanyahu's intent to continue his expansionist and destabilizing policies in the region ahead of elections in Israel."
Turkiye said it supports the establishment of lasting peace in the region, adding that "the sole path to this lies in Netanyahu abandoning his aggressive and coercive policies and demonstrating respect for international law". "Turkey will steadfastly continue its cooperation with the Syrian Government on legitimate grounds to establish peace, stability, and prosperity in Syria, and will never allow Syria to be destabilized," it said.
The remarks came after Israel carried out airstrikes on the Abu al-Duhur military airport in Syria's eastern Idlib province. Israeli Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu's office said that Syria was allowing Turkish troops to deploy at an airbase near Aleppo. Meanwhile, on Tuesday (local time), UN Secretary-General Antonio Guterres' spokesperson Stephane Dujarric called the strikes "yet another very worrying violation" of Syria's territorial integrity and airspace.
Advertisement
"These air strikes should stop, and we stand against them," Dujarric said at a UN press briefing on Tuesday. As per Al Jazeera, Egypt's Foreign Ministry also condemned the Israeli strikes, calling them a "dangerous escalation that threatens security and stability in the region".
In a statement, the ministry said Egypt "fully rejects" Israel's continued violations of Syrian sovereignty and warned that the strikes could further destabilise Syria at a critical time when the country requires support to restore stability and pursue political solutions. Cairo called on the international community to "assume its responsibilities" by putting an end to repeated Israeli violations and adopting firm measures to deter actions that could fuel a broader regional conflict.
Advertisement
Earlier on Tuesday, Israeli Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu's office said Israel and Syria had agreed to maintain a security "status quo". In a post on X, Netanyahu's office said, "Israel and Syria agreed to a status quo in security matters, which Syria was on the verge of breaching by permitting Turkish troops to deploy at an airbase near Aleppo," the statement said.
"Israel will not tolerate threats to its security, and would welcome a return to the status quo," it added. Meanwhile, US Special Presidential Envoy for Syria and Iraq Tom Barrack expressed concern over the Israeli airstrikes, calling them an "unnecessary escalation". "We are deeply concerned that the confirmed Israeli airstrikes on Abu al-Duhur Airbase constitute an unnecessary escalation that does not advance regional stability," Barrack said.
The airbase was targeted in four airstrikes, marking the first reported attack on the facility since the fall of former Syrian President Bashar al-Assad's government in December 2024.

items.title: 'Substantial Progress Made': Canadian PM Carney as American Tariffs Postponed for 3 Days
items.summary: Sharing the remarks in a letter posted on X, Prime Minister Carney reassured that while rigorous engagements remain in place with Washington, Canada remains focused on building a stronger, more independent, and more competitive economy at home.
items.body_text:
'Substantial Progress Made': Canadian PM Carney as American Tariffs Postponed for 3 Days
Sharing the remarks in a letter posted on X, Prime Minister Carney reassured that while rigorous engagements remain in place with Washington, Canada remains focused on building a stronger, more independent, and more competitive economy at home.
- World News
- 2 min read
Ottawa: With Ottawa and Washington continually engaged in discussions over the 50 per cent tariff on a select range of Canadian goods, Prime Minister Mark Carney said that the implementation of the tariffs has been postponed until August 21.
Sharing the remarks in a letter posted on X, Prime Minister Carney reassured that while rigorous engagements remain in place with Washington, Canada remains focused on building a stronger, more independent, and more competitive economy at home.
"Over the last number of weeks, Canada has engaged in intensive discussions with the United States to address outstanding trade issues and deliver greater certainty and real benefits for Canadian businesses, workers, farmers and families," he said.
The Canadian Prime Minister observed that while significant headway has been made, key work remains to be done. Substantial progress has been made, although there is important work still to be done. As this work is ongoing, the United States has agreed to postpone the implementation of its 50% tariff on a range of Canadian goods under Section 338 of the U.S. Tariff Act of 1930 until the end of day, August 21," he said.
Advertisement
The announcement comes in the nick of time as the Trump administration's latest round of tariffs was originally scheduled to take effect at 12:01 a.m. Eastern Time on Wednesday.
According to Canadian public broadcaster CBC, the levies would have applied to hundreds of products worth more than USD 28 billion, from plywood and cement to wine and hockey sticks.
Advertisement
His remarks come shortly after US President Donald Trump on Tuesday (local time) announced a three-day pause on the 50 per cent tariffs on Canadian imports that were due to take effect the following morning, saying the United States and Canada had reached a deal subject to the finalisation of documents.
In a post on Truth Social, Trump said, “I have paused the 50% Tariffs against Canada, that were scheduled to kick in tomorrow morning for a three day period, based on the fact that Canada and the U.S.A., subject to the finalisation of documents, have a DEAL!”
The three-day pause is expected to provide additional time for negotiations between the two countries. Talks intensified last week, with Canadian officials holding discussions with Trump's negotiating team in Washington.

No Need For Pakistani Airspace: India Explores New Flight Route Through China’s Xinjiang
With Pakistani airspace closed to Indian aircraft, New Delhi is exploring a possible route through China’s Xinjiang region for long-haul flights.
- Discussions with China for this route are ongoing.
India is exploring the possibility of using airspace over China’s Xinjiang region as an alternative route for long-haul flights, amid the continued closure of Pakistani airspace to Indian aircraft, according to sources. Sources said the Indian government is examining the feasibility of an alternative corridor through Xinjiang to reduce the impact of the restrictions on flights that would otherwise use Pakistani airspace.
Talks Underway With China
According to sources, discussions between India and China over the proposed route are already underway. Sources in the Civil Aviation Ministry said the Ministry of External Affairs is engaging with Beijing on the matter.
The discussions are understood to have been ongoing for more than a year, although there has been no official confirmation of an agreement or approval for the proposed route so far.

Alternative To Pakistani Airspace
Pakistan’s airspace has remained closed to Indian aircraft for an extended period, forcing airlines to take longer routes on several international services.
The proposed Xinjiang corridor is being considered as another option for long-distance flights. If approved, the route could provide Indian carriers with an alternative to routes affected by the Pakistani airspace restrictions.
Details of the proposed corridor, including which flights could use it and when it might become operational, are yet to be finalised.

items.title: Rain No Barrier! India Win Women’s 4x400m Relay Gold At Asian Games 2026
items.summary: Rain No Barrier! India Win Women’s 4x400m Relay Gold At Asian Games 2026
items.body_text:
India's women's 4x400m relay team won a gold medal at the Asian Games 2026 in Nagoya. They finished first with a time of 3:29.69.
Rain No Barrier! India Win Women’s 4x400m Relay Gold At Asian Games 2026
Asian Games 2026: India won gold in the women’s 4x400m relay at Asian Games 2026, taking its gold medal tally to six and overall medal count to 51.
- India's 4x400m women's relay team secured gold in Nagoya.
- This marked India's first athletics gold of the Asian Games.
- The victory pushed India's overall medal tally past fifty.
Asian Games 2026 Live: India added another gold medal to its Asian Games 2026 tally as the women’s 4x400m relay team delivered a strong performance to finish on top in Nagoya.
The Indian quartet of Kiran, Machettira Poovamma, Prachi and Vithya Ramaraj clocked 3:29.69 to secure the gold medal in the event.
Bahrain finished second in 3:30.21 to take silver, while China completed the podium with a time of 3:31.02. India therefore finished 0.52 seconds ahead of Bahrain in a closely contested race.
India Secure First Athletics Gold Of Asian Games Campaign
The relay victory gave India its sixth gold medal at the 2026 Asian Games and also marked the country’s first athletics gold of the campaign.
India had already collected gold medals in cricket, kabaddi and shooting before the women’s relay team added another title from the track.
The result also took India’s overall medal tally beyond the 50-medal mark. Following the relay gold, India had six gold, 21 silver and 24 bronze medals, taking its total to 51.
The gold also moved India up to 10th place in the overall medal standings.
Vithya Ramaraj Adds Gold To 400m Hurdles Bronze
For Vithya Ramaraj, the relay triumph brought another medal at the Nagoya Asian Games.
The Indian runner had earlier secured bronze in the women’s 400m hurdles. She now has a gold medal to go with that podium finish after helping India win the 4x400m relay.
The Indian quartet also had to deal with difficult weather conditions during the event, with rain affecting the competition.
Despite the wet conditions, India maintained its composure and produced a winning performance to finish ahead of Bahrain and China.
The relay gold adds another significant athletics medal to India’s campaign and takes the country’s overall haul to 51 medals at the Asian Games.

Yes, Vithya Ramaraj also secured a bronze medal in the women's 400m hurdles earlier in the Games. The relay gold adds to her podium finishes.

items.title: BJP Vs Congress Over SIR: Smriti Irani Asks, ‘Why Keep Dead, Duplicate Names In Voter Rolls?’
items.summary: BJP Vs Congress Over SIR: Smriti Irani Asks, ‘Why Keep Dead, Duplicate Names In Voter Rolls?’
items.body_text:
The main conflict is a political battle between the BJP and Congress over the Special Intensive Revision (SIR) of electoral rolls. It escalated with the BJP questioning the Opposition's objections to the Election Commission.
BJP Vs Congress Over SIR: Smriti Irani Asks, ‘Why Keep Dead, Duplicate Names In Voter Rolls?’
Taking aim at the Congress, Irani said the party was targeting the Election Commission instead of reviewing its electoral defeats.
- BJP questioned Congress's objections to electoral roll revision.
- Smriti Irani defended ECI, criticizing Congress attacks and motives.
- Congress leaders demanded CEC Gyanesh Kumar's resignation amidst concerns.
The political battle between the BJP and Congress over the Special Intensive Revision (SIR) of electoral rolls escalated on Tuesday, with BJP leader Smriti Irani questioning the Opposition party’s objections to the Election Commission even as the Congress Working Committee (CWC) stepped up its demands concerning Chief Election Commissioner Gyanesh Kumar.
Addressing a press conference, Irani asked why the Congress wanted the names of deceased people and duplicate entries to remain on electoral rolls.
"Why does Congress want the names of dead people and duplicate names to continue in the electoral rolls?"
Irani also said that the Election Commission strengthens India's democratic system.
"As a citizen, I would like to say that the Election Commission strengthens India's democratic system."
‘Congress Attacking Election Commission Instead Of Reviewing Defeat’
Taking aim at the Congress, Irani said the party was targeting the Election Commission instead of reviewing its electoral defeats.
"The Congress is unhappy that the people of India do not support it within the democratic framework. That is why, instead of reviewing its defeat, Congress is attacking the Election Commission."
She also questioned the Congress' position in states where it is not in government.
"In the states where their government is not in power, is Congress giving the Election Commission a clean chit?"
Irani also referred to remarks made by the Congress national president in 2019.
"In 2019, the Congress national president had said that he would make every effort to tarnish Narendra Modi's image."
She further recalled the Prime Minister's response.
"The PM had said, attack him but do not attack India's democracy and constitutional institutions."

items.title: ‘बहुत पीछे तो नहीं...', राहुल ने ली खड़गे की चुटकी, CWC मीटिंग में मजाक, तंज और राजनीति
items.summary: कांग्रेस कार्यसमिति की बैठक में चुनाव आयोग और SIR को लेकर गंभीर राजनीतिक चर्चा के बीच माहौल कुछ देर के लिए हल्का-फुल्का भी हो गया. राहुल गांधी और कांग्रेस अध्यक्ष मल्लिकार्जुन खड़गे के बीच हुई मजेदार बातचीत पर कमरे में ठहाके गूंजे. वहीं शशि थरूर को लेकर खड़गे की चुटकी ने भी नेताओं के चेहरों पर मुस्कान ला दी.
items.body_text:
