items.body_text:
LAHORE: A judicial magistrate on Tuesday allowed Defence C police a six-day physical remand of two suspects in a case against them over the alleged gang-rape of an Azeri woman.
The 20-year-old Azerbaijan national had travelled to Pakistan for business purposes and was allegedly gang-raped by three men in a rented flat of a private housing society located near Raiwind on the night between Friday and Saturday.
One of the prime suspects had been arrested on Monday, while another’s arrest surfaced on Tuesday. According to Lahore Deputy Inspector General (Investigation) Zeeshan Raza, police had identified the third suspect and were conducting raids to trace him.
On Tuesday, the police produced the two arrested men before Magistrate Azhar Mahmood at Cantonment Courts.
The investigating officer sought their 14-day physical remand for interrogation, collection of evidence and DNA examination.
However, the magistrate approved a six-day physical remand of the suspects.
Separately, a session’s court granted interim pre-arrest bail to a female suspect in the case, restraining police from arresting her till Oct 5.
The Azeri woman had mentioned in her application to the police that two women had approached her for dinner and later they went to a cafe, where the three men accused of raping her had met them.
One of the two women who allegedly approached the victim appeared before the court along with her lawyer on Tuesday.
The lawyer argued that his client had been implicated in the case with mala fide intention. He said she wanted to join police investigation to prove her innocence.
He further expressed fear that she would be arrested and requested the court to approve are pre-arrest bail.
The court granted the suspect bail till Oct 5, with the directive to join the police investigation before the next hearing.
Woman says suspects told her to drink alcohol
The judicial proceedings came a day after the foreign woman recorded her statement before Judicial Magistrate Muhammad Sagheer under Section 164 of the Code of Criminal Procedure (CrPC).
Police Sub-Inspector Faryal Malik, the investigating officer, had produced the woman before the magistrate under strict security arrangements.
In her statement, a copy of which is available with Dawn, the woman said she had arrived in Islamabad from Istanbul on Sept 13 and stayed in Faisalabad for five days before travelling to Lahore.
“I had a plan to visit Skardu, but I could not go there because I was alone,” she said.
According to her, on the day of the alleged incident, she messaged two women, asking them to meet her in Lahore. At around 11pm, she went to a cafe where she met one of them and later accompanied her to a house in Bahria Town to meet the other.
The complainant told the magistrate that at around 2am, a white car arrived carrying two men, one of whom was sent on remand on Tuesday (first suspect).
Later, they moved to an apartment where two more men arrived, one of whom was the second person sent on remand (second suspect), while she did not know the name of the other man.
According to the complainant, in a separate room, one of the women took between Rs20,000 and Rs30,000 from the first suspect, saying the money was for a party, while the second woman also joined them.
The Azeri woman said she made it clear that she “did not need money or alcohol”. She alleged that the first suspect tried to touch her and locked her in a separate room.
When she asked about her friends, she was told that they had left. When she tried to leave, the complainant said she was told that she could not go because her friends had taken money.
The victim said she offered to pay the men, but they told her that she would have to drink alcohol with them before they would let her go.
She alleged that the three men raped her.
She further stated that the suspects then put her in a car and threw her out at an unknown location, while threatening her with dire consequences if she approached the police.

Eight teams have locked in their spots. The first round is a best-of-three, 1-1-1 format, where the better seed hosts Game 1 and, if necessary, Game 3. The best-of-five semifinals started October 4, followed by the best-of-seven WNBA Finals starting October 17.

Taylor Swift fans have been waiting to see her new Patient Zero music video on YouTube since it first premiered at the MTV Video Music Awards.
The video was shown during the awards show over the weekend, but it did not appear on Swift’s YouTube channel right away. This left many fans wondering when they would finally be able to watch it there.

Taylor Nation has confirmed that Patient Zero will be added to Swift’s YouTube channel later today, September 29.
The video stars Colin Farrell, Dakota Johnson and Cara Delevingne, with Swift taking charge as its director. Until now, fans could watch it on music services including Spotify, Apple Music and Amazon Music.
Swift previously explained that she wanted the video to feel dark and mysterious.

"With the Patient Zero video, I got to explore the cinematic and literary genres I love so much. I wanted to incorporate elements of gothic ghost stories, true crime, psychological thrillers all in a setting I hadn’t really shot in much. The house was a metaphor for the coldness of a relationship that’s faded and atrophied," she said.

items.title: Soaring cancer rates emerge as a key US midterms issue
items.body_text:
Soaring cancer rates emerge as a key US midterms issue
- By Reuters -
- Sep 29, 2026
Pacing a stage at the Iowa State Fair, flanked by his wife and four of their six children, Republican US Congressman Zach Nunn spoke passionately about an issue that has emerged as a key concern in his competitive midterms race: cancer.
“Look, my mom is a survivor. I know that it has touched all of us, our family, our friends,” he said at the August event, touting his efforts to bring more money for cancer screening to Iowa’s third congressional district.
Two days before, his Democratic challenger in November’s election, state Senator Sarah Trone Garriott, had discussed cancer on the same stage.
“We know Iowa has a cancer problem. All of us have friends, neighbors, maybe we’ve even experienced it ourselves,” she said.
They were not the only hopefuls to talk about it: five of the six House, Senate and gubernatorial candidates who appeared at the fair discussed Iowa’s high cancer rates, reflecting the extent to which the disease has become a bipartisan campaign issue this year.
Candidates, advocacy groups and strategists say the state’s rising cancer rate – the second highest in the country behind Kentucky – has for the first time emerged as a major issue alongside kitchen-table concerns such as the cost of living.
While the causes of cancer are often complex and not well understood, Iowa voters’ concerns are driven in part by worries that the state’s worsening water pollution from nitrates and other chemicals may be to blame for a spike in cases.
Every major candidate in Iowa’s competitive races for Congress and the state governorship has talked about their plans to tackle cancer in recent speeches, social media posts or on their websites, according to a Reuters review of campaign materials.
The candidates have pledged a range of actions from increasing cancer screening to improving water quality monitoring. Democrats have used the issue to push for expanded healthcare access, while Republicans have promoted greater treatment options and research funding.
After more than a decade of decline, Iowa’s cancer rate began to rise in 2014, and it has had the second-highest cancer rate in the nation since 2023, according to reports by the Iowa Cancer Registry, which tracks and studies cancer cases among Iowans.
It is one of just three states where cancer is rising, driven by higher rates of lung, prostate and breast cancers, among others, according to the National Cancer Institute at the National Institutes of Health.
Tim Hagle, a political scientist at the University of Iowa, said he can’t remember cancer ever being such a significant concern in past elections. The issue has taken hold in part this year because it ties into voter concern about other health issues, like Republican-backed cuts to Medicaid, the federal health program for lower-income Americans, he said.
THE POLITICS OF CANCER
Some Democrats are using the focus on cancer to attack incumbent Republicans for supporting President Donald Trump’s 2025 tax and spending law, which made cuts to Medicaid by expanding work requirements for beneficiaries, among other changes.
Josh Turek, a Democrat running for Senate, in his remarks at the Iowa State Fair criticized his Republican opponent Ashley Hinson, who represents Iowa’s second congressional district, for “(voting) for 110,000 Iowans to lose their healthcare in a state with a cancer and a healthcare crisis.”
Independent health policy research group KFF estimates that around 100,000 Iowans could lose health insurance by 2034 due to changes under Trump’s tax and spending law.
Hinson pointed to her support for legislation that would improve access to mobile cancer screening and mammogram machines in rural areas, and for conservation efforts to improve water quality.
“I have lost two aunts and my grandmother to cancer. It’s personal to me,” she said in an email to Reuters.

items.summary: EU and NATO leaders on Tuesday rallied in support of Estonia and Ukraine after Tallinn accused Russia of "sabotage" in an August arson attack on a drone manufacturer... The post NATO, EU allies rally to Estonia after ‘sabotage’ blamed on Russia appeared first on Iraqi News.
items.body_text:
NATO, EU allies rally to Estonia after ‘sabotage’ blamed on Russia
Tallinn – EU and NATO leaders on Tuesday rallied in support of Estonia and Ukraine after Tallinn accused Russia of “sabotage” in an August arson attack on a drone manufacturer, a claim the Kremlin immediately rejected.
“Russia continues its reckless campaign of hostile actions against NATO allies. It is trying to weaken our resolve and stop our support for Ukraine,” NATO chief Mark Rutte said.
He added: “But Russia is failing. It is failing on the battlefield in Ukraine and it is failing to undermine our unity and support for Ukraine.”
Estonia’s foreign minister, Margus Tsahkna, said an investigation into the August 15 arson attack against the defence company Milrem Robotics, which makes ground drones used in Ukraine, determined that Moscow was responsible.
“We can conclude with certainty that the arson attack… was an act of sabotage ordered by the special services of the Russian Federation,” he said on X.
He said the perpetrators had been arrested, and Russia’s ambassador had been summoned.
Tsahkna said that “this act of sabotage is part of Russia’s broader campaign across Europe, aimed at intimidating us and weakening our support for Ukraine”.
– Kremlin denial –
The Kremlin swiftly dismissed Estonia’s accusation as “baseless” and with “absolutely no relation to reality”.
“We cannot and will not take such statements seriously,” Kremlin spokesman Dmitry Peskov told reporters in Moscow in response to an AFP question.
Estonia has repeatedly accused Russia of hybrid provocations since the beginning of Moscow’s full-scale invasion of Ukraine in 2022.
Along with its neighbours, Latvia and Lithuania, the country has ramped up defence investment and remains a staunch ally of Kyiv.
The European Union said it stood with Estonia calling the arson attack “reckless”, and would not be put off supporting Ukraine.
“Moscow is trying to scare Europe into winding down its support for Ukraine. This will not happen,” European Commission spokesman Christian Wigand said.
French President Emmanuel Macron also called the arson attack a “dangerous escalation” by Russia, and another in a “multiplication of these hostile acts”.
“Russia needs to know that it will not overcome our unity or our determination to continue supporting Ukraine,” Macron said on X.
“Russia’s fingerprints are all over” the Estonia attack, Lithuanian foreign minister Kestutis Budrys wrote on X, adding that Moscow’s “hostile activities do not stop at Ukraine’s borders”.
Latvian President Edgars Rinkevics added that “more support for Ukraine … will be needed and must be provided”.
Swedish Prime Minister Ulf Kristersson called the attribution of the attack “extremely serious” and “directed against Europe as a whole”.

items.body_text:
US grants waiver for Iranian flights at Najaf Airport
Najaf (IraqiNews.com) – An informed Iraqi government source revealed on Tuesday, September 29, 2026, the operational circumstances behind the U.S. administration’s acceptance of an exemption request submitted by Baghdad regarding restrictions on Iranian commercial aviation at Najaf International Airport.
Speaking to Shafaq News Agency, the source explained that while major commercial airports across Iraq rely on international ground-handling contractors bound by U.S. Department of the Treasury directives prohibiting U.S. dollar transactions with Iranian air carriers, Najaf International Airport operates under a distinct administrative model staffed entirely by Iraqi personnel, enabling logistical fee settlements in alternative currencies such as the euro, Iraqi dinar, or Iranian toman.
Administratively detached from the federal Ministry of Transport, Najaf International Airport operates as an autonomous operational directorate under the local government of Najaf Governorate. The facility had continued rendering ground handling, baggage, and refueling services to Iranian airlines until a U.S. Treasury enforcement notice led the Governor of Najaf to issue an administrative directive halting services to avoid exposing the airport to secondary sanctions.
However, following formal representations directed by Prime Minister Ali Faleh Al-Zaidi—who tasked the Minister of Foreign Affairs with negotiating a targeted waiver with U.S. officials—a pathway was cleared allowing the Council of Ministers or the local governorate administration to issue an executive order authorizing the resumption of ground services without triggering international penal measures.
Despite the breakthrough in waiver negotiations, conflicting reports persist on the tarmac regarding immediate flight resumption. While national carrier Iraqi Airways issued a brief statement announcing the restart of scheduled flights to Iranian destinations via Najaf, high-level airport authorities and federal aviation officials confirmed later Tuesday that ground operations for Iranian airlines remain technically paused pending formal ministerial ratification.
Because global ground-handling contractors operating across Baghdad, Erbil, and Basra airports remain barred from processing dollar-denominated aviation fees under U.S. secondary sanctions, Najaf’s sovereign operational structure positions it as Iraq’s primary transit gateway capable of handling bilateral pilgrim traffic and regional commercial flights through non-dollar financial settlements.

items.title: Tensions run high in Northern Ireland after contentious march given go-ahead
items.summary: British Prime Minister Andy Burnham called for calm in Northern Ireland on Sunday after a contentious parade was given the go-ahead by the High Court in Belfast in a late-night sitting. Thousands of protesters, many wearing balaclavas, gathered to block the marchers from the Orange Order, a group hugely supportive of Northern Ireland being part … The post Tensions run high in Northern Ireland after contentious march given go-ahead appeared first on Egypt Independent.
items.body_text:
British Prime Minister Andy Burnham called for calm in Northern Ireland on Sunday after a contentious parade was given the go-ahead by the High Court in Belfast in a late-night sitting.
Thousands of protesters, many wearing balaclavas, gathered to block the marchers from the Orange Order, a group hugely supportive of Northern Ireland being part of the UK, from proceeding down a street in the town of Portadown where many favor unification with the Republic of Ireland.
Fireworks were set off nearby about five minutes before its 8 a.m. start time, and protesters were notified on a loudspeaker that they will be liable for arrest for taking part in an unlicensed counter parade.
Burnham appealed for “calm on all sides” over the parade, saying there have been “big gains made in Northern Ireland, and we don’t want to see things go backwards.”
Sunday’s march marks the first time in almost 30 years that an Orange Order parade has been allowed to go down Garvaghy Road.
The road was a notorious flashpoint before the Good Friday Agreement of 1998 largely ended bloodshed that left 3,600 people dead, some 50,000 wounded and thousands bereaved. In the years before the agreement, there were violent clashes on Garvaghy Road over several summers and requiring major security operations.
Ending the Troubles meant balancing competing identities in Northern Ireland, which remained in the United Kingdom when the rest of Ireland won independence a century ago. Irish nationalists in the north — most of them Catholic — seek union with the Republic of Ireland, while largely Protestant unionists want to stay part of the UK.
Mary Lou McDonald, the president of Sinn Fein, the party historically linked to the Irish Republican Army, said the people of Garvaghy Road would “not be drawn back to the past.”
“This is madness,” she said. “This, in fact, is primitive treatment of any community in the year 2026. It is intolerable, and it will not be tolerated.”
Gavin Robinson, the leader of the Democrat Unionist Party, the largest pro-U.K. party in Northern Ireland, called out Sinn Fein leaders for inflaming the situation.
“The rule of law cannot apply only when Sinn Fein likes the outcome,” he said. “Our institutions are founded on respect for the police, the courts and the rule of law.”
The march was given the final go-ahead at a court hearing which concluded at 2.15 a.m. Sunday.

items.body_text:
In eastern Syria, a man complaining about soaring fuel prices turns to the crowd recording him on their phones and addresses the country’s transitional president.
“We stood with you, so stand with us,” he shouts. “I swear by God, if things don’t change between now and the new year, the situation will turn into something we won’t want. Enough!”
Security officers stand by as he openly denounces the government.
What happens next is striking: nothing.
Earlier this month, thousands of Syrians poured into the streets in the broadest protests since

The protests were widely broadcast on state media, in sharp contrast to Assad’s days, when state television peddled disinformation to discredit them, including claims that the protests were staged from faraway studios in Qatar.
Syria is now navigating the gap between newfound political freedom and an economic recovery that remains frustratingly distant for ordinary citizens, many of whom are losing patience.
The recent demonstrations were sparked by the government’s sudden decision to raise fuel prices by as much as 40%, which it blamed on the global energy crisis caused by the Iran war. As the outrage grew, the government walked back some increases and sent the energy minister before parliament in a show of accountability.
Analysts have praised the government’s responsiveness to its biggest economic stress test yet, but warned it will not change the fundamentals of the country’s cost-of-living crisis. The World Bank assesses that two-thirds of Syrians live below the lower middle-income poverty line, on less than $3.65 a day.
“We’re going to see these protests happening over and over again. It’s virtually impossible to overcome these severe economic challenges that Syrians are suffering. It will gradually become more challenging,” Ibrahim al-Assil, director of the Harvard Kennedy School’s Syria in Transition Lab, told CNN.
That economic strain is causing a growing disconnect between Syrians’ expectations of their new government and their reality.
“The honeymoon period was always going to come to an end. People’s expectations were going to rise, and their patience was going to wear thin if those expectations weren’t met. That’s basically where we are,” said Charles Lister, director of the Syria Initiative at the Middle East Institute in Washington, DC.
Interim President Ahmed al-Sharaa is racing to rebuild Syria – an estimated $216 billion task – before patience runs out. He inherited a nearly bankrupt state that was plundered by Assad and his cronies, leaving the new regime largely reliant on foreign investment.
His strategy has been to bring the country back onto the global stage after decades of isolation, and he is now trying to turn that international momentum into tangible economic gains.
“Syria has restored its status into the international community. It has been a transit for the world. We also built diplomatic bridges and we proved to the world that the security of the region has to start in Damascus,” al-Sharaa told the UN General Assembly on Wednesday.
The global embrace of al-Sharaa is perhaps best embodied by his warm rapport with US President Donald Trump, who he has met four times since last May. The outcome has been the complete lifting of all US sanctions on Syria, the key to unlocking foreign investment.
Turkey, Qatar, Saudi Arabia and the United Arab Emirates have driven most foreign investments thus far, estimated by Syria last year at $28 billion. The European Union has committed $2.7 billion in support, and French President Emmanuel Macron signed several new economic, transport and infrastructure agreements during a July visit to Damascus.

items.summary: OpenAI said it won’t release its latest model, dubbed GPT-6.1 Astra, because it “didn’t quite meet the bar” for safety. The decision, which the Wall Street Journal first reported on Monday, comes as industry leaders call for an AI development slowdown. Anthropic CEO Dario Amodei first proposed “pacing the frontier” earlier this month in an … The post ‘Didn’t quite meet the bar’: OpenAI won’t release new AI model due to safety concerns appeared first on Egypt Independent.
items.body_text:
OpenAI said it won’t release its latest model, dubbed GPT-6.1 Astra, because it “didn’t quite meet the bar” for safety.
The decision, which the Wall Street Journal first reported on Monday, comes as industry leaders call for an AI development slowdown. Anthropic CEO Dario Amodei first proposed “pacing the frontier” earlier this month in an essay published online, to which OpenAI CEO Sam Altman and other executives agreed to commit to imposing more safeguards.
OpenAI describes its Astra model on its website as “state-of-the-art on computer use, browsing, professional work, software engineering, cybersecurity, and science.”
There are trade-offs regarding AI safety, said Saachi Jain, OpenAI’s head of safety systems, in a statement to CNN. AI safeguards require a balance of “staying within scope” and “avoiding laziness” when models work towards tasks, he said.
“While (GPT-6.1 Astra) improved on axes such as model laziness, it didn’t quite meet the bar in terms of staying within scope and authorization, and how it communicates back to the user about the type of work it’s done,” said Jain.
He added that there is an “extremely high bar” regarding safety when AI models are made available to consumers. GPT-6.1 Astra was set to debut in October, according to the Journal. The company will continue to release other models in the future.
“Of course we want to make sure our model development is safe no matter whether that’s in the company, or when we ship it to users,” said Jain.
Concerns regarding AI safety have escalated since this summer, when OpenAI revealed in July that its agents escaped a testing environment and breached AI startup Hugging Face. Competitors Anthropic, Meta and Google have also said their agents were involved in separate breach attempts.
OpenAI has been investigating agents’ use of internet access since the Hugging Face breach, and recently reported that agents targeted government websites in the United States and Australia.
CNN’s Hadas Gold contributed to this report.

items.body_text:
Supply Ministry postpones bread price review amid ongoing push from bakeries, mills          
        Supply Minister Sherif Farouk has asked for a week’s review period before the ministry responds to a request to raise its guideline consumer prices for two categories of non-subsidized bread, according to a source who was present at a Sunday meeting where representatives from bakeries and mills put forward their request.
The request is their second in just a few months, following a dispute over the extent of the ministry’s role in setting and enforcing non-subsidized bread prices.
Their push for higher guideline prices comes as the industry’s production costs rise steadily, with wheat prices spiralling again amid an escalation in the intensity of Russia’s war on Ukraine, and as domestic fuel prices continue to rise against the backdrop of the regional war.
Farouk said the ministry would review price movements over the coming week, and, if prices did not fall over that period, the ministry would revise guideline prices for the tourist and fino bread categories, the source said. The ministry did not commit to a specific percentage increase.
Senior representatives of the General Bakeries Division raised the issue of production costs at the meeting and called for a review of tourist and fino bread prices, proposing a 15 percent increase.
Milling sector representatives also presented an update on the wheat and flour markets and recent pressures on production costs, particularly higher maritime shipping and logistics costs and rising global wheat prices amid the shipping disruptions in the Black Sea.
Imported wheat reached record prices at the beginning of this week, rising to between LE16,600 and LE16,800 for Ukrainian wheat and LE17,000 for Russian wheat, compared with a maximum of LE12,200 to LE12,500 per ton in June.
Bakeries selling tourist bread rely on the free market for their flour supplies, which account for more than 50 percent of production costs, the source said. Transport and other operating costs have also risen, leaving bakeries facing significant losses.
The meeting is the latest in a series of calls bakeries have made to the ministry regarding tourist and fino bread prices, which intensified in August as flour and other production costs increased.
The Supply Ministry did not respond to the demands, issuing a directive instead on August 4 to maintain the prices and weights for tourist and fino bread set in March.
As bakeries continued to call for price increases, sources in the sector questioned the legal basis for the imposition of mandatory pricing on tourist bread, whose production inputs are not subsidized.
Lawyer Khaled Ali previously told Mada Masr however that since wheat is a “strategic commodity,” the ministry has a role in market oversight.
The ministry also threatened legal action against violators of its price directives at the time, with Interior Ministry statements later announcing “large scale campaigns to control supply crimes” against those violating Supply Ministry decisions on prices and weights.
The changes in wheat and flour prices come amid volatility in global wheat markets, particularly continued tensions in the Black Sea region, the main source of Egypt’s wheat imports. Import data for the first eight months of the year showed that Russia and Ukraine together accounted for more than 82 percent of Egypt’s wheat imports, despite repeated announcements by the Supply Ministry of plans to diversify import origins.

items.body_text:
Govt tells BP it would block sale of company’s Egypt assets to Energean          
        The government informed British Petroleum it would reject a deal that would see the British company sell some of its Egypt based oil and gas assets to Israeli majority-owned Energean, according to two sources informed of the deal who spoke to Mada Masr on condition of anonymity, one of whom who works for the company.
The stance was communicated during a meeting in Cairo on Thursday between Petroleum Minister Karim Badawy and BP Executive Vice President Gordon Birrell, they said.
One reason the government gave for rejecting the potential deal was “national security imperatives,” according to the BP source. Other concerns relate to the wide gap in technical capabilities between the two companies, particularly in deep water drilling, an area where Energean’s capacity is comparatively limited, the source said.
The meeting came as BP seeks to divest part of its energy asset portfolio in Egypt, while the government is pushing to attract more investment into the petroleum sector in order to raise natural gas production amid a major energy shortfall.
Media reports have pointed to exclusive talks between BP and Energean over the latter’s purchase of some of BP’s assets in Egypt, although no deal has been officially announced.
Any change in ownership of oil fields between producing companies requires the approval of the government, represented by the Egyptian General Petroleum Corporation. EGPC holds pre-emption rights, with agreements between companies and the government stipulating that any transfer of rights must first be offered to EGPC or receive its approval before being transferred to a third party, according to the two sources, as well as to a former EGPC official and former head of the Electricity Utility and Consumer Protection Regulatory Agency, Hafez al-Salmawy.
The BP source anticipated that the company’s next move could see it officially announce the deal and its talks with Energean on Wednesday, despite knowing that Egypt intends to reject it. But BP also has the option to wait until it has a clearer picture, the source said.
If BP does reach a final agreement with the Israeli company, it will have to formally apply to the Egyptian government, through EGPC, for approval as a condition of completing the deal.
According to the second informed source, an official announcement from BP would act as a maneuver to pressure EGPC, as it would clearly mark the assets covered by the deal as up for sale, something that might hold up further investment decisions for those assets. This would be particularly sensitive in the case of the Temsah concession, which includes the Denise West field, where a finding of an estimated two trillion cubic meters of natural gas reserves was announced earlier this year.
The government is undertaking a push at present to increase domestic gas production, which has fallen to its lowest level in a decade, while domestic demand continues to grow. Gas prices have also risen significantly, putting pressure on the state budget.
Reuters cited informed sources to report at the end of August that BP, which produces around 60 percent of Egypt’s natural gas, had entered exclusive talks with Energean to acquire the assets the British company wants to sell. The potential deal has since sparked broad controversy, including questions submitted by several members of Parliament to the Petroleum Ministry.
The lawmakers specifically sought reassurances regarding Energean’s “financial solvency, technical expertise and operational capacity,” to ensure that the new foreign partner would be able to inject enough to finance the drilling and development programs required of it at the Egyptian fields.

items.title: With region in turmoil, Madbuly, Abdel Atty go to UNGA

items.body_text:
With region in turmoil, Madbuly, Abdel Atty go to UNGA                    
                As diplomats and heads of states from around the world descend on New York this week to hold official and unofficial talks during the United Nations General Assembly, the already-long ledger of regional crises continues to grow.
In recent weeks the Houthis have taken key areas overlooking the crucial Bab al-Mandab Strait, triggering renewed fighting in Yemen. Meanwhile in Ethiopia, the long-simmering tensions in Tigray have boiled over, with the Tigray People’s Liberation Front seizing on Wednesday the restive northern state’s three airports and setting the stage for what could become another complex regional war in the Horn of Africa.
This is in addition to the continued war in Sudan, the threat of escalation in Iran, the dire oil crisis that the continued closure of the Strait of Hormuz has created, and the stalled diplomatic process on Gaza.
Egypt finds itself at the intersection, if not directly involved in many of these crises. To represent Egypt’s position at the mega-diplomatic forum that is the UNGA, President Abdel Fattah al-Sisi called on Prime Minister Mostafa Madbuly for the second year in a row to lead Cairo’s delegation.
Sisi led Egypt’s delegations to the UNGA himself from 2014 to 2019. Since then, he has sent his foreign minister in his place: first Sameh Shoukry, who held the post from 2014 to 2024, and now Badr Abdel Atty.
The president’s decision to not personally lead the delegation this year, according to a government official, comes down to the fact that he “did not want to personally participate in the meeting of the Board of Peace, even though the primary issue on the agenda was Gaza — a pivotal matter for Egypt.”
“To this day, the board remains unable to take serious action to improve the situation for Palestinians on the ground — despite a full year having passed since the ceasefire agreement between Hamas and Israel, following two years of an Israeli war of extermination against Gaza — which is, of course, deeply embarrassing for Cairo,” the government official says.
The Board of Peace, chaired by United States President Donald Trump, was established earlier this year, with Bulgarian diplomat Nickolay Mladenov selected as the board’s envoy to the Gaza Strip. According to a member of the National Committee for the Administration of Gaza — a body established by the Board of Peace to succeed Hamas — the board is “completely powerless to even secure Israel’s consent for the committee to enter the Strip, or to allow the exit of 10,000 individuals selected for training in Egypt to serve as a Palestinian police force replacing Hamas’s police, even though Hamas has publicly declared its readiness to relinquish all its weapons.”
Although a source with direct insight into Egyptian-Israeli relations states that Cairo is maintaining all official and unofficial communication channels with Tel Aviv to address the situation in Gaza, this does not imply that the head of government will personally participate in Board of Peace meetings, given its limited effectiveness.
Instead it was Madbuly who led the delegation to the Board of Peace meetings to discuss the situation in Gaza on Wednesday.
Setting aside what a member of the team preparing for the Egyptian delegation’s visit to New York described to Mada Masr as Madbuly’s largely ceremonial role, much of Egypt’s political messaging is being handled by Foreign Minister Badr Abdel Atty, whose schedule has been packed with meetings. Egypt’s top diplomat arrived in New York on September 19 — two days before Madbuly — and is set to return to Cairo next week.
According to the team member, there are four key issues atop Abdel Atty’s agenda during his meetings in New York. The first is the situation in Sudan.

Arab African International Bank (AAIB) has expanded its employee training framework over the past three years to prepare more than 3,000 staff members for future leadership roles and develop the next generation of CEOs, the bank said.
The bank recently marked the graduation of members of its senior management team from Harvard Business School’s Senior Executive Leadership Program.
“AAIB is a destination for learning and development. When an opportunity presents itself, be ready,” AAIB’s vice chairman and managing director said during the celebration.
Arab African International Bank’s expanded educational framework provides employees with technology and innovation learning opportunities through the Massachusetts Institute of Technology (MIT), alongside access to Udemy Business, an artificial intelligence-powered digital learning platform.
To complement external partnerships, AAIB has launched several internally developed initiatives. These include the AI Champions Program, the Gamified Simulation League, specialised academies, and an internal rotation programme named “The Catalyst”.
The Arab African International Bank’s training agenda also incorporates interactive experiences focused on exploring how artificial intelligence can enhance the workplace, which are designed to reinforce critical thinking and informed decision-making among employees.

items.title: AngloGold Ashanti plans further investment in promising Egyptian mining sites
items.summary: President Abdel Fattah Al-Sisi said Egypt is seeking to expand its partnership with AngloGold Ashanti, operator of the Sukari gold mine, to cover exploration, technology transfer, and local supply-chain development, as the company announced plans for additional investment in several promising mining sites in Egypt without disclosing the value or timing of the spending. Al-Sisi […]
items.body_text:
President Abdel Fattah Al-Sisi said Egypt is seeking to expand its partnership with AngloGold Ashanti, operator of the Sukari gold mine, to cover exploration, technology transfer, and local supply-chain development, as the company announced plans for additional investment in several promising mining sites in Egypt without disclosing the value or timing of the spending.
Al-Sisi made the remarks during a meeting with AngloGold Ashanti Chief Executive Alberto Calderon on the sidelines of the fifth Egypt Mining Forum 2026, attended by Prime Minister Mostafa Madbouly and Petroleum and Mineral Resources Minister Karim Badawi, according to a presidency statement.
Al-Sisi said the government was keen to support AngloGold Ashanti’s investments in Egypt and provide an environment that would enable its operations to expand, stressing Cairo’s interest in broadening the relationship beyond the operation of Sukari.
The presidency said the proposed partnership would cover expanded exploration activities, technology and expertise transfer, training for Egyptian workers, development of local supply chains, and efforts to attract additional investment to the mining sector.
Calderon reviewed the company’s operations and expansion plans in the Egyptian market and said Egypt was one of AngloGold Ashanti’s priority investment destinations.
He said the company planned to invest further in several promising mining areas, which could support the discovery and development of new projects similar to Sukari, according to the presidency.
The two sides also discussed expanding AngloGold Ashanti’s exploration programmes, particularly in gold mining. Al-Sisi said the government would provide the necessary support to facilitate the company’s activities as part of Egypt’s strategy to increase mining’s contribution to the economy and attract greater foreign investment.
Earlier, Al-Sisi opened the Egypt Mining Forum, which brought together representatives of governments, international organisations, and major foreign companies operating in the sector.
During the opening session, Al-Sisi said the state was committed to supporting the success of investors and companies operating in mining and other sectors.
The forum featured speeches from officials at the Ministry of Petroleum and Mineral Resources, AngloGold Ashanti, the Australia-Africa Minerals and Energy Group, the International Council on Mining and Metals, and the World Bank Group, as well as live broadcasts from mining sites across Egypt.
Al-Sisi also opened the exhibition accompanying the forum and toured stands belonging to the Ministry of Petroleum and Mineral Resources and companies including Capital Drilling, Elsewedy Electric, and AngloGold Ashanti.

items.title: Egypt’s Finance minister targets Qatari energy and tourism investments during Doha talks
items.summary: The minister of finance stated he is seeking to increase Qatari investments in the energy and tourism sectors, while targeting more diverse financing tools to stimulate private investment in developmental projects. During a meeting with Qatari Minister of Finance Ali bin Ahmed Al Kuwari on the sidelines of the Asian Infrastructure Investment Bank (AIIB) meetings […]
items.body_text:
The minister of finance stated he is seeking to increase Qatari investments in the energy and tourism sectors, while targeting more diverse financing tools to stimulate private investment in developmental projects.
During a meeting with Qatari Minister of Finance Ali bin Ahmed Al Kuwari on the sidelines of the Asian Infrastructure Investment Bank (AIIB) meetings in Doha, Minister Ahmed Kouchouk said that expanding bilateral partnerships enhances the private sector’s role in economic activity, drives growth, and creates jobs.
Kouchouk emphasised the government’s aim to encourage joint projects between Egyptian and Qatari companies to achieve more sustainable economic growth for both nations. The ministers also discussed joint cooperation between their respective finance ministries to exchange expertise and enhance capacity in fiscal and tax policies.
In a separate AIIB session titled “Financing for Impact,” Kouchouk told attendees that transforming economic reforms into real investments contributes to more sustainable growth. He noted that the government is proceeding with economic reforms in parallel with social protection measures to support the most vulnerable groups.
Public-private partnership projects represent the “natural evolution of infrastructure investment,” with a specific focus on the sustainable and renewable energy sectors, the minister said.
Stimulating investments in new and renewable energy will contribute to enhancing the competitiveness of Egyptian exports, Kouchouk stated. He added that the ongoing development of roads, ports, and logistics, coupled with customs reforms, supports the country’s transformation into a regional trade hub.
To fund these initiatives, the minister highlighted the need for a greater role for multilateral development banks, which he said can help transform reforms and developmental projects into actionable investments.
Kouchouk pointed to the issuance of “Panda bonds” as a successful model for innovative financing. He noted that guarantees provided by development banks help attract more investors, and that the state aims to utilise more diverse financing tools and guarantees to stimulate private sector participation in development projects.

items.title: Why Did Syrian Pragmatism Stop at the Relationship with Iran?
items.summary: The question of the future of Syrian-Iranian relations returned to the fore after remarks by Iranian President Masoud Pezeshkian, Syria TV writes. The post Why Did Syrian Pragmatism Stop at the Relationship with Iran? first appeared on The Syrian Observer.
items.body_text:
Since the fall of Bashar Al-Assad’s regime on December 8, 2024, the new Syrian government has redrawn its network of foreign relations on a wide scale.
Damascus opened up to Arab countries, Turkey, the United States, and Europe. In a step that stirred a degree of controversy, it also reopened a page with Russia, which was among the most prominent political and military backers of the Assad regime and whose forces took part directly in the war after its military intervention in 2015.
But this Syrian pragmatism has so far stopped at Iran. Relations between the two countries have remained frozen, despite nearly two years since the fall of the ousted regime. During that time, the new Syrian government has been busy reviving Syrian diplomacy and working under a balance-of-power theory, through strong relations with the main international and regional actors and with other states of economic or geopolitical importance.
The question of the future of Syrian-Iranian relations returned to the fore after remarks by Iranian President Masoud Pezeshkian in an interview with Al Jazeera from New York in September 2026. He said his country had not been able so far to establish a relationship with the new Syrian government because of what he described as “the impression they created.”
He expressed hope that Damascus would act on the basis of “Islam, religion, justice, and fairness,” adding that working according to religion and the Sunnah of the Prophet, in his view, would remove the problem.
The Syrian response came quickly from Mohammad Al-Jafal, adviser for Afro-Asian affairs at the Syrian Foreign Ministry. He tied the possibility of establishing future relations with Tehran to the latter’s review of its policies and its respect for Syria’s sovereignty.
In a statement to the Syrian Arab News Agency (SANA) on Sunday, Mr. Jafal affirmed that Damascus’s position on Iranian policy is not tied to a passing political circumstance. He said it rests on an experience spanning about 14 years, during which, according to him, Iran supported the ousted Assad regime through the years of war in Syria.
He said Tehran’s alignment with the former regime contributed to complicating the Syrian crisis and increasing Syrians’ suffering, adding that this background cannot be bypassed when discussing the future of relations between the two countries.
He explained that Syria today follows a policy open to countries around the world but does not see the possibility, at the same time, of ignoring what the country witnessed over the past years or bypassing Syrians’ rights.
Mr. Jafal added that any Iranian move to build a new relationship with Damascus should be based on respect for the sovereignty of the Syrian state and the will of its people, along with a review of past policies and work to rebuild trust between the two sides.
The Syrian official stressed that Syria is “not an arena of influence for any country” and that its foreign relations will be built on mutual respect, national interests, and equality. He affirmed that Damascus does not seek hostility with any country, nor does it accept subordination to any party, but looks forward to building balanced relations that respect its sovereignty and its people’s choices.
The new Iranian statements appear to have forgotten or ignored what the Iranian regime did over 13 years in Syria, as if nothing had happened. Meanwhile, some try to present Russia and Iran as equivalent in their political and military backing of the regime against the Syrian Uprising.
In truth, Russia was not far from the Syrian war, and its intervention was no less impactful. It is in fact well known that it came at Iran’s direct coordination and request, after the enormous losses the regime suffered at the hands of rebel factions. But the matter grows more complicated when we get into the details. items.title: Aleppo Citadel Launches “Touristech” Project to Digitize Heritage Visits
items.summary: According to Minister Salhani, artificial intelligence will be part of this vision in the coming phase - not as a substitute for humans, but as a tool for analyzing markets, improving the visitor experience, and directing investments. The post Aleppo Citadel Launches “Touristech” Project to Digitize Heritage Visits first appeared on The Syrian Observer.
items.body_text:
Aleppo Citadel hosted the launch event for the “Touristech” project on Sunday, September 27. The project uses technology to promote Syrian heritage and improve the visitor experience, and it coincided with World Tourism Day celebrations.
The event, which Enab Baladi attended, was held under the patronage of the Ministry of Tourism and the Aleppo governorate, with the participation of Minister of Tourism Mazen Al-Salhani and Aleppo Deputy Governor Ali Hanoura. It was organized by the International Junior Chamber (Beroya) and the Northern Region Tourism Chamber, in cooperation with the Directorate of Antiquities and Museums, and sponsored by the Qatani Group.
The program included performances by Circassian, Armenian, and Kurdish troupes, along with a heritage revival troupe, as part of an effort to highlight the cultural diversity that distinguishes the city of Aleppo.
What Is the “Touristech” Project?
According to the project’s introductory presentation during the ceremony, “Touristech” aims to change how archaeological sites are visited, starting with Aleppo Citadel, without altering anything tied to the sites’ identity or history. Instead, it uses technology to bring history closer to visitors and make it clearer and more interactive.
The project turns a visit to the citadel into a journey with multiple stops. At each stop, visitors can learn the story of the place through interactive units and screens, and they can also use a QR code to access additional information and materials, including photos, maps, and site-related content.
As a result, the visitor’s experience is not limited to viewing an archaeological site. According to the presentation, it helps visitors understand what happened there, who passed through, and why the site gained its historical importance.
The experience does not begin at the citadel gate, as the project also includes an online platform and an open digital archive for Aleppo Citadel.
The platform allows access to the project’s content from anywhere before, during, and after a visit, with the aim of presenting the citadel’s history in a simpler and more accessible form.
The content is offered in Arabic and English, given that the story Aleppo Citadel carries is not limited to the city’s residents but forms part of Syria’s history and heritage.
Moving Toward “New Tourism”
During the ceremony, which Enab Baladi attended, Minister Salhani said that tourism is an engine of the economy, a space where cultures meet, and a source of job opportunities.
According to Minister Salhani, the choice of “Digital and Artificial Intelligence to Redesign Tourism” as the theme for World Tourism Day reflects the future direction of the sector.
He said the challenge lies in turning archaeological sites into sustainable economic value that benefits citizens, society, and the state.
He pointed to what he described as tangible achievements in the recent period, including a return to growth in arrivals, the reopening of a number of tourist facilities, and a rising pace of rehabilitation and investment.
According to him, these indicators are not merely dry figures but reflect a return of confidence and the tourism sector’s ability to recover.
On investment, Minister Salhani said the ministry has moved to managing projects by controlling economic returns and protecting public funds, and has launched what he described as high-caliber projects. He said these reflect a shift toward building integrated tourist destinations rather than settling for individual tourist facilities.
Minister Salhani added that the ministry does not want Syria to return to old-style tourism. Instead, it is working to establish a new tourism based on quality before quantity, one that treats the local community as a partner in development rather than a recipient of its effects.

items.title: Real Estate Projects in the Crosshairs of Protests – Who Will Settle the Expropriated Land File?
items.summary: Residents of Qudsaya suburb stopped work machinery at the "Sham View" project on Saturday, al-Hal writes. The post Real Estate Projects in the Crosshairs of Protests – Who Will Settle the Expropriated Land File? first appeared on The Syrian Observer.
items.body_text:
In Rural Damascus, the new real estate development projects around Qudsaya and Dummar no longer face only the test of implementation and investment. They have entered a direct confrontation with an older issue: ownership of land that its owners say was expropriated under the former regime, without their rights ever being definitively settled.
In the latest move, residents of Qudsaya suburb stopped work machinery at the “Sham View” project on Saturday. They demanded that work halt until the legal status of the properties covered by the project is clarified and their owners’ situations are settled.
Protests to Halt the Two Projects
The move coincided with a demonstration attended by dozens of residents of Qudsaya, Dummar, Al-Bajaa, Moadamiya, and other areas of Rural Damascus. It set out from the square in Qudsaya suburb toward the offices of “Sham View” and then “Abyat Hills.”
The protesters demanded a halt to both projects on land they say was expropriated, a reconsideration of the expropriation decisions, and access for property owners to their holdings. They also called for the compensation and ownership file to be settled before development work proceeds.
The protests come as real estate activity in the area accelerates. The General Housing Establishment, in partnership with the Saudi Thra Company for Real Estate Development and Investment, launched the “Sham View” project on an area of about 178 hectares. It includes more than 10,000 real estate units, among them 7,500 residential units, along with commercial and hotel units, schools, and service and cultural facilities. On September 22, the establishment announced the opening of subscriptions for the first phase, which covers 2,000 units, with deliveries set to begin in 2029.
The Core of the Objection
“Abyat Hills” is being developed by the Saudi company Abyat in partnership with the General Housing Establishment. It is located in Qudsaya suburb on an area of about 380,000 square meters and includes more than 2,000 residential units. The company also launched the “Modern Urban Cluster” project in Al-Bajaa, with about 20,000 units. Investment in the two projects exceeds USD 2 billion.
The core of the objection is a legal question that the official statements published on the two projects have not settled. It concerns the fate of the previously expropriated land, the purpose for which it was expropriated, and whether the owners’ rights and compensation were settled before the land was brought into new investment projects. Under Legislative Decree No. 20 of 1983, public bodies may expropriate real estate to carry out projects of public benefit. The decree also regulates the procedures for assessing and paying compensation and the means of objection and appeal.
The issue also carries a constitutional dimension. Article 16 of the Syrian Constitutional Declaration provides for the protection of private property, which may not be taken except for the public interest and in return for fair compensation.
While the government presents the new projects as part of expanding the housing sector and attracting investment, landowners demand that the ownership file be settled before construction begins.
So far, the published official statements do not give a detailed account of the ownership of all the properties included in the two projects, or of how the protesters’ demands will be addressed. This leaves the expropriation file an open point of contention between the real estate investment track and the rights of the former owners.

items.title: Trump backs strategy to ease Russia sanctions in exchange for release of political prisoners
items.summary: The Atlantic reports that Donald Trump backed envoy John Coale's strategy to ease Russia sanctions in exchange for political prisoner releases.
items.body_text:
Trump backs strategy to ease Russia sanctions in exchange for release of political prisoners
The Atlantic has reported that US President Donald Trump's special envoy John Coale has proposed a new strategy towards Russia that would seek the release of political prisoners in exchange for easing sanctions and resuming economic ties with Moscow.
Source: The Atlantic, as reported by European Pravda
Details: The Atlantic says Trump has backed the idea.
The outlet notes that Coale tested this approach in Belarus: after hundreds of political prisoners were released, the US eased sanctions and began talks on purchasing Belarusian potash.
Coale now wants to apply this model to Russia.
US officials are also considering major business deals with Russia as part of a strategy to achieve peace.
The US is also seeking to broker a limited ceasefire in Russia's war against Ukraine, covering strikes on energy infrastructure and shipping in the Black Sea. However, Russia continues to attack Ukraine, and Ukrainian officials do not expect serious peace talks to take place in the near future.
Under Coale's plan, the release of political prisoners and a gradual resumption of trade could create new channels of dialogue between the US and Russia and encourage the Kremlin to end the war. Critics of the strategy fear that exchanging the release of political prisoners for sanctions relief could instead encourage authoritarian regimes to take more people hostage.
On Monday, the White House nominated Coale for the position of special presidential envoy for hostage affairs with the rank of ambassador. The position requires Senate confirmation.
Asked to comment on his mission, a White House official said: "The president and his team remain committed to continuing to play a constructive role in ending the war between Russia and Ukraine, and he remains optimistic that we'll ultimately get a peace deal done."
Coale plans to coordinate his efforts with Steve Witkoff, who is Trump's main point of contact in relations with the Russian side.
Background:
- The New York Times previously reported that the White House is considering signing certain business deals with Russia as a way of demonstrating its good intentions.
- Russia has previously tried to entice Trump with the potential benefits of economic cooperation, discussing joint projects involving rare-earth mineral and aluminium extraction, projects in the Arctic and the involvement of US companies in selling Russian natural gas to Europe.

Polish PM warns of very difficult months ahead for Poland due to Russia's aggressive stance
Polish Prime Minister Donald Tusk has warned of "very difficult weeks and months" ahead for Poland due to Russia's increasingly aggressive actions towards Ukraine.
Source: Polish news channel TVP Info, as reported by European Pravda
Details: Tusk said at a government meeting on 29 September: "Very difficult weeks and months lie ahead of us, given Russia's increasingly aggressive stance towards Ukraine, and unfortunately, these aggressive actions by Russia towards Ukraine are coming increasingly close to our border."
Meanwhile, he said the government and the appropriate services are focused on ensuring that the threat does not spread to Polish territory and that "nothing bad happens on the Polish side".
Tusk also commented on an incident that occurred near the Dorohusk-Yahodyn border crossing between Poland and Ukraine on 28 September, when a Russian drone struck on the Ukrainian side near the Polish border.
"Every night or during the day, we are forced to repeatedly scramble our aircraft, as Russian attacks near the Polish border, specifically at border crossings and infrastructure near the border, have now become a permanent occurrence," the Polish prime minister said.
He added that the appropriate Polish services are on heightened alert due to the situation along the country's eastern border.
Background:

items.title: Tusk: Poland prepares for difficult months ahead amid Russia's growing aggression
items.summary: Polish Prime Minister Donald Tusk stated that the coming weeks and months will be difficult for Poles due to Russia’s increasingly aggressive actions against Ukraine, which are drawing closer to the Polish border.
items.body_text:
Tusk: Poland prepares for difficult months ahead amid Russia's growing aggression
The head of the Polish government made this statement on Tuesday before the start of a meeting of the Council of Ministers of the Republic of Poland, according to a Ukrinform correspondent.
“We have very difficult weeks and months ahead of us due to Russia’s increasingly aggressive stance toward Ukraine, and, unfortunately, these aggressive actions by Russia against Ukraine are getting closer and closer to our border,” Tusk noted.
According to him, Russian attacks near the Polish border—particularly near border crossings—have already become a regular occurrence.
“Every night or every day, we have to scramble our air force multiple times, as Russia’s attacks near the Polish border—specifically on border crossings and infrastructure near the border—have already become a regular occurrence,” the Polish prime minister stated.
Tusk noted that on Monday, one of the Russian drones crashed near the Yahodyn-Dorohusk border crossing on the Ukrainian side of the border.
The head of the Polish government assured that the government and relevant agencies are focused on “ensuring that nothing bad happens on the Polish side of the border.”
At the same time, Tusk emphasized the good cooperation with Ukraine. According to him, the Ukrainian side promptly informs Poland about threats and attempts to shoot down Russian drones while they are still over Ukrainian territory.
“We can count on—as was the case last night—immediate notification and the actions of the Ukrainians, who are trying not only to report that something is flying toward Poland but also to neutralize this threat while it is still over Ukrainian territory,” the Polish prime minister emphasized.
As reported by Ukrinform, Poland scrambled military aircraft the day before in response to a Russian attack on western Ukraine. An alert was declared in Poland’s Lublin Voivodeship, which borders Ukraine.
The Supreme Commander of NATO’s Allied Forces in Europe, Alexus Grinkevich, stated on Monday that the best response by European countries to Russian sabotage and other destabilizing actions should be to publicly acknowledge Moscow’s responsibility and strengthen support for Ukraine.
Photo: Office of the Prime Minister

items.title: EU Might Press Ukraine on Reforms to Unlock Billions in 2026 Aid
items.summary: EU leaders are expected to press Ukraine to move faster on reforms linked to financial support for 2026, according to a draft seen by Rapporteur. The proposed wording comes as Kyiv and Brussels weigh urgent funding needs against new wartime tax measures.
items.body_text:
EU leaders may use their October summit to urge Ukraine to accelerate reforms tied to billions of euros in financial support, according to an early draft of the meeting’s conclusions seen by Rapporteur.
The draft calls on all parties, “notably Ukraine,” to step up work needed to release funding under the €90 billion ($102 billion) Ukraine Support Loan and the Ukraine Facility in 2026, according to Rapporteur, formerly known as Euractiv.
JOIN US ON TELEGRAM
Follow our coverage of the war on the @Kyivpost_official.
Of the €45 billion ($51 billion) in loan funding earmarked for this year, €14.9 billion ($16.9 billion) has been disbursed so far.
The outlet said delays include the Ukrainian parliament’s failure to adopt the anti-corruption and tax measures Brussels sought. The draft could change before leaders meet on Oct. 15-16.
The pressure comes as Ukraine seeks more money to cover the rising cost of its defense as Kyiv stares down a $27 billion funding gap. Kyiv has also asked for part of its EU loan funding to be brought forward so it can place drone orders this autumn, President Volodymyr Zelensky said last week.
But Finance Minister Serhiy Marchenko questioned whether Ukrainians should face higher taxes now. Speaking at a European Policy Centre event on Monday, he pointed to the strain Russian strikes and disrupted trade have placed on households and businesses.
Among the measures Brussels considers at risk, according to an internal document cited by Rapporteur, are taxes on low-value imported parcels and income earned through digital platforms.
Russian Military Personnel Gap Widens
Ukrainian lawmakers initially rejected the parcel tax reform on Sept. 1 before passing it in its first reading alongside the introduction of simplified insolvency procedures for micro, small, and medium-sized enterprises (MSMEs) close to two weeks later.
The parcel tax would introduce a 20% value-added tax (VAT) on cross-border e-commerce parcels valued at under €150 ($170), bringing in an estimated Hr.10 billion ($224 million) annually. It must pass its second reading and await the president’s signature to become law.
A European Commission spokesperson said on Monday that financing and reforms needed to move forward together to support Ukraine’s resilience and its path toward EU membership. Marchenko is due to discuss the country’s funding needs with international donors in Brussels.

items.title: Russian Military Personnel Gap Widens
items.summary: Zelensky says Russia is ramping up recruitment, conscripts, foreign mercenaries & N. Korean troops to plug severe manpower gaps from heavy losses. Putin ordered a small force increase; ISW warns voluntary enlistment fails & involuntary call-ups loom as casualties outpace recruits by thousands monthly.
items.body_text:
Ukrainian President Volodymyr Zelensky in a Monday evening national video address said the Kremlin’s military was intensifying recruitment and incorporating mercenaries into the Russian Armed Forces in an attempt to fill chronic personnel shortages at the front.
Zelensky stated on Sept. 28:
JOIN US ON TELEGRAM
Follow our coverage of the war on the @Kyivpost_official.
“Today I received a report from the Defense Intelligence [Ukraine’s military intelligence agency, Головне управління розвідки, or HUR] on the steps Russia is planning next. In practical terms, the Russians have begun new mobilization of conscripts. They are increasing the number of people that they take in [into the military] by various means. They are planning to increase recruiting for foreigners.”
More than 8,000 North Korean soldiers are currently on Russian Federation territory assisting in operations against Ukraine, and Pyongyang is training another 10,000 soldiers to reinforce them, Zelensky said, adding:
“Russia is paying for all of this by various illicit means, and in return, for this this help, for the technical assistance by Russia on North Korean territory, there has been set up a production line for Shahed-type strike drones. This is how evil works together, and how a deadly threat in one end of the world becomes a deadly threat in another end of the world.”
Countries from which Russia recruits foreign soldiers to fight as mercenaries in Ukraine should work with Kyiv and international law enforcement agencies to prevent that, Zelensky said.
EU Might Press Ukraine on Reforms to Unlock Billions in 2026 Aid
Western states also should intensify sanctions against Russia and states cooperating with Russia, because if unchecked, the Kremlin’s attacks against Ukraine and other countries will only increase, Zelensky said.
Zelensky’s comments followed a Monday order by Russian leader Vladimir Putin for a limited increase in the size of his country’s armed forces, and a decree instructing military recruiters to work harder to find men for the Russian Armed Forces.
The Presidential order raised by 15,500 the size of Russia’s armed forces to a total of 2,441,630 personnel, including 1,550,500 military personnel, and directed state funding be funneled to intensified recruitment.
It was the fourth increase in military personnel ordered by the Kremlin in 2026 alone. In 2022, the Kremlin faced with a collapse of its pre-war professional military caused by unexpectedly heavy casualties among mobilized reservists.
The executive decree published on the Presidential register made no mention of increased conscription or mobilization of reservists. In the run-up to national elections earlier in the month, some Kremlin critics had suggested the moment voting was over the Putin regime would implement a wide-ranging draft forcing tens of thousands of civilians into the military to fight in Ukraine.
Putin in early September called reports he was planning to mobilize reserves “utter nonsense” (Russian: “чушь собачья”) and during a Sept. 3 speech in Vladivostok told an audience, “There is no scenario today that would require mobilization… from the point of view of availability of military service members, Russia has no problems whatsoever.”
According to both tracking by the Ukrainian Armed Forces (AFU) and international military observers, Russian forces operating in Ukraine are suffering heavy and sometimes devastating losses in attacks most often carried out by unsupported infantry soldiers ordered to traverse open terrain under continuous observation by Ukrainian drones. According to those sources, Russian personnel shortages are severe and, thus far, Kremlin efforts to fill shortfalls have been insufficient.
According to data published by the Icelandic-based researcher Ragnar Gudmundsson on Tuesday, two days in Sept. 2026 saw some of the highest daily losses by Russian forces of the entire war (Sept. 28 – 2,090 men, Sept. 17 – 1,960 men).

items.title: ‘We Need to Survive’: Zelensky’s Hometown Faces Budget Cuts After Factory Shutdowns
items.summary: Kryvyi Rih plans to revise its budget after the shutdown of major industrial employers reduced tax revenue. City defense council head Oleksandr Vilkul blamed Russian attacks and difficulties exporting through ports.
items.body_text:
When a steel plant stops in Kryvyi Rih, the losses reach far beyond its factory gates. Fewer shifts mean less work for contractors, lower tax receipts for the city and less money for the services residents rely on.
That chain of losses is now forcing the hometown of President Volodymyr Zelensky to cut its municipal budget and postpone some development projects, according to Oleksandr Vilkul, head of Kryvyi Rih’s defense council.
JOIN US ON TELEGRAM
Follow our coverage of the war on the @Kyivpost_official.
However, he said the city would prioritize keeping schools, kindergartens, hospitals, water supplies, and heating systems running.
Vilkul said ArcelorMittal Kryvyi Rih, the Inhulets and Southern mining and processing plants, and the Kryvyi Rih Iron Ore Plant were all idle. Other major businesses were producing at no more than a quarter of their prewar levels leaving many companies that supply or service them without work.
He blamed Russian strikes and difficulties shipping products through ports. The operating status of the other plants was not independently verified.
ArcelorMittal confirmed last week that it could not safely restart its Kryvyi Rih operations. The company said its facilities had been hit four times in five weeks, most recently on Sept. 21.
Five employees were killed and 17 injured in those attacks, with production facilities suffering extensive damages. ArcelorMittal said it would focus on preserving the site so a future restart would remain possible.
Estonia Slams Russian ‘Sabotage’ After Arson Attack on Defense Company
For the city, the immediate concern is both employment and the budget. Vilkul said industrial taxes pay for public-sector wages, infrastructure maintenance, pipe and boiler-house repairs, and social services. He described next year’s budget outlook as poor, though he did not give a figure for the planned cuts or identify which projects would be delayed.
“But this isn’t about development. It’s about survival. Right now, we have to survive,” he said.
Vilkul said municipal utilities had been asked to help displaced industrial workers find jobs. The city’s water and heating companies currently have around 1,000 vacancies between them.

Александр Плющенко — сын генерального директора и совладелицы академии «Ангелы Плющенко» Яны Рудковской и олимпийского чемпиона Евгения Плющенко. Спортсмен выступает за Азербайджан. В текущем сезоне он дебютировал на этапах Гран-при среди юниоров, заняв 13-е место в Анкаре и десятое в Батуми.

items.title: В поставках нефти с Ближнего Востока наметился перелом
items.body_text:
В сентябре 2026 года экспорт нефти с Ближнего Востока резко вырос, приблизившись к тому уровню, который наблюдался до закрытия Ираном Ормузского пролива. Об этом сообщило The New York Times (NYT).
Предполагается, что это восстановление может ослабить давление на мировые цены на энергоносители. Издание сослалось на данные компании Kpler, согласно которым в первом месяце осени через Ормузский пролив ежедневно проходило в среднем 10 миллионов баррелей нефти. Через трубопроводы и порты, обходящие пролив, ежедневно из стран Персидского залива вывозилось шесть миллионов баррелей сырой нефти. До начала войны с Ираном в конце февраля из региона ежедневно по морю и другими путями вывозилось около 19 миллионов баррелей нефти.
Есть мнение, что увеличение экспорта нефти свидетельствует о возможном ослаблении контроля Ирана над этим водным путем.
Ранее сообщалось, что Саудовская Аравия возобновила экспорт нефти по ключевому трубопроводу «Восток — Запад». Он был отремонтирован после ударов беспилотников в начале сентября.

items.title: The Atlantic: Трамп согласился ослабить санкции против России
items.summary: Президент США Дональд Трамп согласился ослабить санкции против России в обмен на освобождение заключенных, сообщает The Atlantic. Механизм предложил посланник американского президента в Восточной Европе Джон Коул, заключивший аналогичную сделку с властями Белоруссии.
items.body_text:
The Atlantic: Трамп согласился ослабить санкции против России
Президент США Дональд Трамп согласился ослабить санкции против России в обмен на освобождение заключенных, сообщает The Atlantic. Механизм предложил посланник американского президента в Восточной Европе Джон Коул, заключивший аналогичную сделку с властями Белоруссии.
Фото: Kevin Lamarque / Reuters
По сведениям издания, предложение посланника возникло после его встречи с российским журналистом Дмитрием Муратовым (объявлен в РФ иноагентом). Стороны обсудили создание механизма, аналогичного сделке между Вашингтоном и Минском. Господин Коул уже составил список американцев, содержащихся в тюрьмах России, а господин Муратов (объявлен в РФ иноагентом) — осужденных россиян, которые выступали против боевых действий России на Украине.
Параллельно с переговорами об освобождении заключенных Вашингтон планирует обсуждать с Москвой торговые и деловые вопросы. Они могут касаться нефти, дизтоплива и редкоземельных минералов. Как отмечает The Atlantic, вчера Белый дом выдвинул кандидатуру Джона Коула на должность спецпосланника президента по делам заложников. Теперь ее должен утвердить Сенат. Комментируя решение, в Белом доме заявили, что «привержены конструктивной роли» в прекращении украинского конфликта.
Власти США стали смягчать санкции в отношении Белоруссии в обмен на освобождение заключенных. В середине сентября Минск согласился освободить 25 заключенных в обмен на снятие санкций с двух белорусских компаний, включая производителя калийных удобрений «Беллесбумпром». Дональд Трамп вскоре анонсировал сделку с Белоруссией по закупке удобрений. В переговорах по сделке, по сведениям The Atlantic, участвовали российские представители. Россия ранее уже освобождала заключенных оппозиционеров в рамках обмена с Западом. Крупнейший из них состоялся в августе 2024 года, в нем участвовали 26 человек.
В белорусском случае обмен санкционных уступок на освобождение заключенных строился поэтапно. В сентябре 2025 года освобождение 52 человек сопровождалось снятием санкций с авиакомпании «Белавиа». Позднее, после освобождения 250 человек, США обещали вывести из-под рестрикций ключевые белорусские банки, Министерство финансов, а также компании «Беларуськалий» и Белорусскую калийную компанию. Предметом уступки были конкретные компании и финансовые структуры в обмен на определенный объем освобождений.
Экономический эффект такого смягчения ограничен санкциями других участников: пока Европейский союз сохраняет запрет на транзит белорусских калийных удобрений через Литву, прежние объемы экспорта быстро не восстановятся. Освобождение заключенных также само по себе не означает прекращения политических репрессий или изменения внешнеполитического курса Белоруссии.

items.title: Вышла книга «Мы никогда не умрем. Кто придумал 2007-й»
items.summary: Вышел труд Николая Овчинникова и Владимира Завьялова «Мы никогда не умрем. Кто придумал 2007-й: ню-метал, эмо, металкор — краткая история тяжелой альтернативы в России».
items.body_text:
Вышла книга «Мы никогда не умрем. Кто придумал 2007-й»
Вышел труд Николая Овчинникова и Владимира Завьялова «Мы никогда не умрем. Кто придумал 2007-й: ню-метал, эмо, металкор — краткая история тяжелой альтернативы в России». На первый взгляд после взлета отечественного альтернативного рока прошло не так много времени, чтобы определять его место в истории. Однако для авторов книги «Мы никогда не умрем» оно очевидно. Они пишут: «Остатки этого облака сейчас питают постсоветскую поп- и рок-сцену — от Little Big до ATL, от "Кишлака" до "Спасибо"». А позднее Николай Овчинников замечает: «Когда я слушаю Джизуса или "Три дня дождя", я слышу отголоски песен… с первого альбома "Психеи"».
Авторы «Мы никогда не умрем» рассказывают и об истоках российской волны — о западной альтернативной музыке, прежде всего о ню-метале, ставшем ориентиром для героев книги. Там была своя «большая тройка»: Korn, Linkin Park, Limp Bizkit. Популярности Limp Bizkit и им подобных способствовал спрос на «бедного белого человека» из рабочего класса, на мужчину со своими чувствами и трещинами. Герои ню-метала — буквально олицетворение выражения «хрупкое мужское эго»: орут про маскулинность, но на самом деле плачут в подушку.
Подробнее — в материале «Ъ» «Прочтите мне мой 2007-й».
2007 год в этой истории важен как обозначение периода, когда тяжелая альтернатива получила собственную инфраструктуру. Рекорд-лейблы, клубы и телеканалы создавались почти с нуля и работали слабо связанно с прежней музыкальной индустрией, что позволило сцене самостоятельно превращать слушателей массовой музыки в поклонников новых групп.
Кризис 2008 года изменил формат и команду телеканала, ориентированного на эту музыку, но не отменил уже достигнутого эффекта: за три года сформировалось поколение, для которого тяжелая альтернатива стала музыкальной базой. Ее влияние на последующую поп- и рок-сцену связано именно с этим накопленным опытом слушателей и собственной системой распространения музыки.

items.title: Шесть человек погибли при крушении военного самолета Ту-95 в Амурской области
items.summary: Стратегический бомбардировщик Ту-95 потерпел крушение в Амурской области при выполнении учебно-тренировочного полета, заявило Минобороны России. По предварительным данным, погибли шесть членов экипажа, еще один госпитализирован.
items.body_text:
Шесть человек погибли при крушении военного самолета Ту-95 в Амурской области
Стратегический бомбардировщик Ту-95 потерпел крушение в Амурской области при выполнении учебно-тренировочного полета, заявило Минобороны России. По предварительным данным, погибли шесть членов экипажа, еще один госпитализирован.
Как уточнило ведомство, самолет выполнял полет без боекомплекта. Он упал в безлюдной местности. Для установления причин крушения к месту катастрофы вылетела комиссия Воздушно-космических сил России.
По данным источников «Ъ», катастрофа произошла вблизи села Красноярово вскоре после взлета бомбардировщика с аэродрома Украинка. Причиной крушения, по предварительным данным, стала техническая неисправность. Возбуждено уголовное дело по ст. 351 УК РФ (Нарушение правил полетов или подготовки к ним).
Украинка — крупный военный аэродром дальней авиации в Сарышевском районе Амурской области. Он расположен в 26 км севернее города Белогорска. В июле ФСБ России заявила, что Служба безопасности Украины готовила теракт на аэродроме Украинка с использованием FPV-дронов со взрывчаткой.
Подробнее — в материале «Ъ» «Украина против Украинки».
