items.title: Four places to visit in Germany this autumn
items.summary: This month marked the official end of summer in Europe and the northern hemisphere. With temperatures getting cooler, autumn is the perfect time to explore Germany and check out some of its more unusual festivals.
items.body_text:
It's quieter for a start and the new season brings a feast of russet browns and flame reds to leaves on trees. It's also typically the time when events start to ramp up again after the summer break. Here are four places to explore this autumn.
Lichtenberg in Berlin
If you're thinking of heading to Berlin, autumn is the perfect time for a trip – it gets colder, but not yet freezing.
But before you head straight for the city centre, you might want to explore Berlin's 11th borough, Lichtenberg. Home to a museum of East Germany's secret police in their former headquarters, it's also where you'll find the Landschaftspark Herzberge.
This 100-hectare park used to be a freight train hub, but it's now a haven of varied trails through densely wooded pastures studded with black Pomeranian sheep, orchards, ponds and pools.
This year will mark the 37th anniversary of the fall of the Berlin wall and this year the city is marking the occasion with a series of events that it's calling Freedom Week.
The long open-air East Side Gallery that was once part of the Berlin Wall is on most people's lists when they visit the city. This November 9th (and surrounding dates) will be filled with art, tours, screenings and more events designed to take participants back to 1989 when people worked together to bring down the dictatorship in the GDR.
October 3rd is also a national holiday in Germany for 'Reunification Day'.
READ ALSO: 10 things you never knew about German reunification
Neustadt in Rhineland-Palatinate
Some excellent wines come out of Germany and the Palatinate region is no exception. In fact, it's one of Germany's largest and best-known growing regions. It's also home to The German Wine Harvest Festival (Weinlesefest). Think of a smaller, infinitely more chilled version of Munich's Oktoberfest but with the focus on wine, and you'll kind of get the picture of the annual September-October event.
READ ALSO: Four reasons to visit a German wine fest this year
Over 100,000 people descend on the secret wine capital of Neustadt every year for the event which celebrates Thanksgiving. You'll find a 'wine village' with hundreds of local wines to taste, live music, a funfair, and, of course the grand finale – a huge wine procession with newly elected 'Wine Queens' leading an array of colourful floats.
Part of Germany's 'Wine Route' that takes you on an epic journey through historic vineyards and stunning countryside, the medieval city is well worth exploring in its own right for its picture-perfect half-timbered houses and cobblestone streets.
The grape harvest is in full swing at this time of year, so it's a great time to visit the local sun-kissed vineyards in the neighbouring wine villages and, of course, taste their wines.
Cologne in North Rhine-Westphalia
Think of Cologne and a city of art and culture, a gothic twin-spired cathedral and its famous carnival, one of Europe's largest, probably come to mind.
While the full parade of floats and street festivities isn't until February/March, the carnival actually officially opens on November. To be precise, at 11 minutes past 11 on the 11th month, ie November. Get ready for the so-called fifth season!
Carnival societies, beer halls and other venues across the city hold colourful parties featuring DJs playing well-known Kölsch (or Cologne) music and carnival bands like Bläck Fööss and Höhner, while more traditional ones present the Dreigestirn, the three men (yep, the maiden is traditionally portrayed by a man, too) who've been bestowed the titles of maiden, prince and peasant by the festival committee for the occasion. Alaaf!
Weimar in Thuringia
How do you like those onions? No, really, are you an onion fan? If you are, you'll love the 370-year-old Zwiebelmarkt (onion market) in the Thuringian city of Weimar on the second weekend of October every year.
Starting out as a cattle and onion market, the three-day festival is dedicated solely to the humble vegetable now.

items.title: What are Munich's plans for the Olympic Games?
items.summary: From the Olympiapark to a new housing area in Daglfing via various events across Bavaria, we look at how Munich and the surrounding area would be transformed for the Olympic and Paralympic Games.
items.body_text:
Munich has just been selected as Germany's candidate to host the 2036, 2040 or 2044 Summer Olympic and Paralympic Games.
Should the Bavarian capital’s bid succeed against international competition, urban planners, citizens and politicians are hoping it will provide a major boost for the city.
Other regions – such as Augsburg, Bad Wiessee, the district of Erding and Lake Starnberg – are also hoping to benefit from the event.
READ ALSO: Germany selects Munich for Olympics host bid
Olympiapark to take centre stage
The Munich bid centres on the Olympiapark, or Olympic Park, in the north of the city. Built for the 1972 Games, it has undergone extensive renovations in recent years.
The site is used for both elite and grassroots sport, as well as for concerts. For several years, it has also been home to the SAP Garden, a 12,500-seat indoor arena which also serves as the home of Munich’s professional basketball and ice hockey teams.
If Munich gets the green light, almost half of the sports venues would be located in the Olympic Park. These include traditional sports such as athletics, alongside newer sports like 3x3 basketball.
According to planners, 90 percent of the sports venues would be situated within a 30-kilometre radius of the Olympic Village.
Competitions for the Paralympic Games would use the same venues as the Olympics. The bid says this is intended to ensure barrier-free routes for athletes and spectators, and give Paralympic sports the same visibility.
Munich Mayor Dominik Krause, of the Greens, called the bid a "highly sustainable Olympic concept". He added: "No other Olympic host city could offer this kind of post-Games use."
Where else would events take place?
As was the case at the 2022 European Championships in Munich, other sports would be spread across the city and held at existing venues, similar to the 2024 Games in Paris.
The plan is for dressage to take place in front of Nymphenburg Palace, as it did in 1972, and archery in front of Schleißheim Palace, while open-water swimming would be held in Lake Starnberg.
The bid foresees boxing at the exhibition centre, rugby at the Grünwalder Stadium and badminton at the Rudi-Sedlmayer-Halle.
Under the proposals, swimming events would be held at a temporary pool installed inside a planned event area near Munich airport.
View this post on Instagram
Outside Munich, the canoe slalom would be held at the Augsburg Eiskanal.
Football would be played in Nuremberg, Regensburg, Stuttgart and Karlsruhe, while the sailing competitions would take place in Kiel, as they did in 1972, and all the mountain bike cross-country events would be held in Bad Wiessee on Lake Tegernsee.
The new Olympic and Paralympic Village is planned for the Daglfing area. After the Games, it is set to be repurposed as climate-neutral and accessible housing for more than 10,000 people. Here, too, Paris serves as a model, having created an entirely new urban district in Saint-Denis for the 2024 Summer Olympics.
Of course, there is still plenty of renovation work on the cards if Munich wins the bid – for example at the grandstands for the rowing and canoeing regatta course in Oberschleißheim.
What is Munich's track record for hosting?
The Bavarian capital has become accustomed to hosting major sporting events in recent years.
In the 10 days leading up to the DOSB's decision on September 26th, Munich was chosen as the host of the 2028 Champions League final – having done so in 2012 and 2025 – along with the 2031 World Athletics Championships.
Munich's Allianz Arena was selected to host the first regular-season NFL match on German soil in 2022 and will do so for a third time in November.
Since the last time the Summer Games were on German soil in 1972, Germany has launched seven unsuccessful bids to play host.

items.title: Painting could become standard disaster recovery therapy: Minister
items.summary: Coordinating Minister for Community Empowerment Muhaimin Iskandar stated that painting could become a standard ...
items.body_text:
"Painting can become the standard for the psychological recovery of children in disaster-affected areas. This could become a model and a mandatory budget item for the government to provide space for artistic expression as a therapy in disaster handling," Iskandar said here on Tuesday.
He said painting could serve as a natural outlet for expression, especially for children who are victims of natural disasters.
He noted that paintings produced through this recovery program would tell a much more meaningful story, since they stem from experiences that cannot be replaced even by technology.
In addition, paintings could generate economic added value for affected communities through appreciation such as exhibitions and auctions held by communities or art collectors.
He also said post-disaster recovery programs involving painting would give rise to new artists who could enrich Indonesia's creative talent pool.
"This extraordinary added value will benefit appreciation efforts, especially for emerging artistic potential, which can grow while also gaining economic value from the creative economy," he said.
He also praised the program run by the Creative Economy Ministry to provide space for children who are disaster victims in Aceh, North Sumatra, and West Sumatra to produce paintings as part of the Rekon Rehab recovery program.
Iskandar said creative economy players must be given space to build their capacity and develop economic potential, both from art and other creative products, that can revive regional economies, especially in disaster-affected areas.
"One example we will continue to develop, especially in Aceh, is reviving Aceh's coffee, which has gone global and become our national pride. We will continue to carry out environmental and economic recovery," he added.

items.title: Govt targets drug inmate rehab to ease prison overcrowding
items.summary: President Prabowo Subianto has instructed Law Minister Supratman Andi Agtas to formulate a comprehensive rehabilitation ...
items.body_text:
"I was specifically asked to coordinate with several ministries and agencies—including the Head of the National Narcotics Agency (BNN), the Head of the National Research and Innovation Agency (BRIN), and other ministers—to devise a rehabilitation plan targeting drug users inside correctional facilities," Supratman said after a limited cabinet meeting at the Presidential Palace Complex in Jakarta on Tuesday.
The directive comes in response to severe overcrowding across the national prison network.
Data from the Directorate General of Corrections as of April 2026 shows that prisons and detention centers nationwide house over 271,000 inmates against a capacity of approximately 146,000, resulting in an overcrowding rate of about 85 percent.
Official records as of May 4, 2026, indicate that 146,284 inmates, or 53.9 percent of the national prison population, are incarcerated for narcotics-related offenses.
BNN Head Suyudi Ario Seto noted that his agency will work closely with relevant ministries to define the criteria and mechanisms for providing medical and social rehabilitation to incarcerated users.
"We will hold a more in-depth coordination meeting regarding rehabilitation efforts, specifically concerning users or inmates involved in narcotics cases who have been processed and detained but still require rehabilitation," Suyudi stated.
In addition to prison reform, Minister Supratman reported to the President progress on legal aid accessibility, highlighting the establishment of roughly 83,960 community legal aid posts (posbankum) across villages and urban communities nationwide.
Out of approximately 16,000 complaints received by these posts, around 14,000 cases were resolved through mediation using a restorative justice approach, while the remaining two thousand are receiving free legal aid services.

items.title: Nanning Friendship Cities Conference Highlights AI, Connectivity and Cultural Tourism
items.summary: The 2026 Nanning-Hanoi Economic Corridor and Belt and Road Nanning Friendship Cities Conference was held in Nanning, ...
items.body_text:
Nanning, China (ANTARA/Xinhua-AsiaNet)- The 2026 Nanning-Hanoi Economic Corridor and Belt and Road Nanning Friendship Cities Conference was held in Nanning, south China's Guangxi Zhuang Autonomous Region, on Sept. 18, bringing together government, business and academic representatives from several countries and regions.
The Publicity Department of Nanning City noted that under the theme "Empowering Cities with Digital Intelligence, Connecting for a Shared Future," the conference focused on artificial intelligence, the Pinglu Canal and cultural tourism.
With the continued development of the New International Land-Sea Trade Corridor, the signing of the China-ASEAN Free Trade Area 3.0 Upgrade Protocol and the opening of the Pinglu Canal, cooperation between Nanning and ASEAN cities is gaining new momentum in trade, logistics, the digital economy and people-to-people exchanges.
Zhong Dezhi, deputy secretary of the CPC Nanning Municipal Committee and acting mayor of Nanning, said the city hopes to deepen cooperation with its international friendship cities in connectivity, trade, artificial intelligence, culture, tourism and youth exchanges.
This year marks the 20th anniversary of friendly ties between Nanning and Hai Phong, Vietnam. Hoang Minh Cuong, vice chairman of the Hai Phong People's Committee, said Hai Phong looks forward to stronger cooperation with Nanning in digital transformation and logistics, while expanding youth, cultural and tourism exchanges.
Artificial intelligence was a key focus of the conference. Participants discussed how digital technologies can support urban governance, industrial development and international cooperation. The Nanning International Friendship Cities AI Industry Cooperation Alliance was also launched to promote exchanges and industrial cooperation among partner cities.
The Pinglu Canal also featured prominently in discussions. The canal is expected to strengthen links between Nanning, the Beibu Gulf ports and ASEAN markets, while creating new opportunities for logistics, trade and tourism.
Nanning is also exploring canal-based tourism products, including sightseeing passenger routes and cultural experiences, linking transport connectivity with tourism development.
The Publicity Department added that cultural tourism was another major area of cooperation. Participants discussed tourism route development, visitor exchanges and cultural programs, with a focus on strengthening people-to-people ties among friendship cities.
A number of cooperation projects were signed during the conference, further expanding Nanning's partnerships with international friendship cities, particularly those in ASEAN.

items.title: Unmatched EJ Obiena shatters Asian Games record to defend throne
items.summary: EJ Obiena delivers the Philippines' third gold medal in the 2026 Asian Games as he breaks his own record to repeat as men's pole vault champion
items.body_text:
MANILA, Philippines – When it comes to Asia, EJ Obiena is in a league of his own.
And he reinforced that notion as Obiena defended his Asian Games crown following a record-breaking performance in men’s pole vault at the Nagoya City Mizuho Park Athletic Stadium in Japan on Tuesday, September 29.
Obiena set a new Asian Games mark after clearing 5.91 meters in a single attempt, delivering the Philippines’ third gold medal in this edition after gymnastics star Carlos Yulo won the first two in artistic gymnastics.
He shattered his own record of 5.90m, which Obiena set in 2023 when he won his first Asian Games title in Hangzhou, China.
After two failed attempts at 5.80m, Obiena upped the ante by going for 5.91m, which he surpassed with room to spare on the way to becoming the first back-to-back champion in the event since Kazakhstan’s Igor Potapovich won in 1994 and 1998.
It marked the first time Obiena cleared over 5.90m since he posted 5.97m in ruling the Irena Szewinska Memorial in 2024.
Two Chinese bets completed the podium, with Yao Jie and Li Chenyang bagging silver and bronze, respectively, with 5.70m clearances.
Obiena highlighted the Philippines’ best athletics showing in decades, with the country also bagging a pair of bronze courtesy of John Cabang Tolentino (men’s 110m hurdles) and Victoria Bossong (women’s 800m). – Rappler.com

items.title: COA finds ‘unverifiable’ beneficiaries in DepEd’s SHS voucher program
items.summary: The dozens of unverifiable beneficiaries of the senior high school voucher program resulted in an overpayment of P938,000, according to state auditors
items.body_text:
AT A GLANCE
- The Commission on Audit identified 58 unverifiable beneficiaries of the Department of Education's senior high school voucher program, leading to an overpayment of P938,000 for the school year 2025-2026.
- The unverifiable beneficiaries included students who dropped out, transferred, were not enrolled, deceased, or absent during validation, highlighting deficiencies in beneficiary validation and monitoring by the DepEd.
- In response to the findings, the DepEd has tightened its validation and accountability measures and has begun recovering overpayments.
MANILA, Philippines – There were 58 “unverifiable” beneficiaries of the Department of Education‘s (DepEd) senior high school (SHS) voucher program, which resulted in an overpayment of P938,000 in school year (SY) 2025-2026, the Commission on Audit (COA) found.
According to COA’s compliance audit on the existence and eligibility of voucher beneficiaries, the flagged unvalidated beneficiaries were:
- 32 students who had officially or unofficially dropped out
- 12 who transferred to other schools
- 11 who were not enrolled in the second semester
- 2 who were reported deceased
- 1 who was absent during validation with no records available
The overpayment of P938,000, which was for 53 out of the 58 unverified beneficiaries, had already been released to their respective schools, COA said in its 2025 annual audit report on the DepEd released last September 23.
Four beneficiaries were excluded from billing statements prior to payment as of February, while the subsidy for one beneficiary had not yet been released as of March.
Moreover, state auditors found five beneficiaries who were “misclassified under incorrect voucher categories,” resulting in an overpayment of P14,710.
Other deficiencies seen were incomplete or improperly maintained supporting documents and inadequate monitoring by the DepEd and the Private Education Assistance Committee, which helps in implementing the Government Assistance to Students and Teachers in Private Education (GATSPE).
“These lapses expose the program to the risk of erroneous billing and overpayment, compromise the reliability of beneficiary validation, and may result in the disbursement of funds to ineligible beneficiaries, contrary to the objective of providing financial assistance exclusively to qualified learners,” COA said.
The SHS voucher program is a government financial subsidy program for qualified Grades 11 and 12 students. It provides assistance in the form of vouchers ranging from P14,000 to P22,500 per year, which are paid directly to the student’s chosen private school.
COA said the program’s participating schools are responsible for encoding and updating student information.
“The status of the concerned [voucher program beneficiaries] should have been duly updated and subjected to DepEd verification to prevent potential overpayments,” the commission added.
On Tuesday, September 29, the DepEd said it had acted on the COA findings.
“As part of its five-layer validation, DepEd, through its co-manager of the senior high school voucher program, Private Education Assistance Committee, has completed its school year 2025-2026 validation. Through this year-end validation, flagged cases are being reviewed and confirmed overpayments will be recovered,” part of the DepEd’s statement read.
The agency said it had “tightened beneficiary validation, billing, refund, and accountability measures” in the revised Expanded GATSPE guidelines released in April.
The DepEd said it will “continue to pursue accountability and the recovery of government funds where warranted.”
Issue of ‘ghost students’
The DepEd investigated 12 private schools in February 2025 over the alleged presence of ghost students in the SHS voucher program.
By March 2025, the agency recovered P65 million from the voucher program amid irregularities, with 38 private schools fully refunding the government.
In July 2026, the DepEd said a regional trial court had sentenced an individ

items.title: Victoria Bossong claims 800m bronze in Asian Games debut
items.summary: The fastest in the heats, Victoria Bossong finishes third in the women's 800 final as she delivers the Philippines' second athletics medal in the 2026 Asian Games
items.body_text:
MANILA, Philippines – Victoria Bossong turned in a slower time in the final but still salvaged an athletics medal for the Philippines in the 2026 Asian Games as she snagged the bronze in the women’s 800m at the Nagoya City Mizuho Park Athletic Stadium in Japan on Tuesday, September 29.
The Filipina-American middle-distance specialist clocked 2 minutes and 5.34 seconds to finish third and deliver the Philippines’ second athletics medal in this edition of the quadrennial showpiece after John Cabang Tolentino bagged bronze in the men’s 110m hurdles.
China’s Wu Hongjiao struck gold with 2:04.49, while Bahrain’s Nelly Korir clinched silver with 2:05.16 — the three medalists separated only by less than a second.
Bossong, whose mother, Catalina Atienza, hails from Oriental Mindoro, emerged as the title favorite after posting the fastest time in the heats, where she registered 2:02.34.
A repeat of that time would have netted the 23-year-old Harvard University graduate the Philippines’ first Asian Games gold medal in a track event since the late Lydia de Vega ruled the women’s 100m in the 1986 edition.
But it simply was not meant to be for Bossong, who owns a personal best of 1:58.52 — a time that eclipses the Asian Games record of 1:59.02 set by Kazakhstan’s Margarita Mukasheva in 2014.
Still, Bossong enjoyed a promising debut for the Philippines in a multi-sport event, which came just months after she gained eligibility in July to represent the country. – Rappler.com

MANILA, Philippines — The Energy Regulatory Commission (ERC) has adopted a new format for consumers’ monthly electricity bills to reflect the allowable system loss charges that were earlier declared exempt from value-added tax (VAT).
In a press release on Tuesday, September 28, the state’s electric power agency said distribution utilities are required to “clearly and separately” break down all the government-mandated pass-through charges in the new bill format.
The new bill format was approved by the ERC through Resolution No. 28, series of 2026, during a commission meeting held on September 16.
In the new bill format, the allowable system loss charges are separately identified and excluded from gross sales for VAT computation.
“The new format will make it easier for consumers to distinguish between charges subject to VAT and government-mandated pass-through charges excluded from VAT,” the ERC said in a statement.
The adoption of the new billing format comes after the Bureau of Internal Revenue (BIR) formally removed the 12% VAT on allowable system loss charges in September as part of the government’s efforts to cut the electricity bills paid by consumers.
Standardized ‘other charges’
Aside from the new bill format, the ERC has also passed Resolution No. 30, series of 2026, to adopt uniform rates on “other charges” that distribution utilities may collect from their consumers.
“The new framework aims to make these charges more transparent, consistent with the applicable regulatory principles, and directly tied to the actual cost of providing specific services,” the ERC said.
Under the new policy, distribution utilities may impose and collect the “other charges” only on specific customer-requested and account-related services, such as connection, disconnection, and reconnection services.
It also formalized the computation for “other charges,” including only the direct labor, deployment and fuel, and replacement materials that were directly used for providing service. Other administrative-related costs, meanwhile, are excluded from the computation.
“For consumers, this means greater protection against double charging. Costs already recovered through ERC-approved Distribution, Supply, and Metering rates cannot be collected again from the Other Charges,” the agency added.
Late payment rules
Late payments were also covered in the ERC’s resolution, saying that they must also be identified as a separate item by the distribution utilities in the new bill format.
According to the agency, distribution utilities may only charge their consumers 2% of either the current month’s bill or the unpaid portion, depending on which is lower, for the late payment fee.
The distribution utilities were also reminded to properly issue a Notice of Disconnection to consumers in case of nonpayment.
The distribution utilities are given 90 days to adjust their billing and other systems.
“They must also make the uniform schedule of charges accessible through their bulletin boards, official websites, and other official social media platforms,” the ERC said.

items.title: Lord Allan Velasco out of Philippines, BI confirms
items.summary: No hold departure order or derogatory record prevented the ex-speaker's exit.
items.body_text:
Lord Allan Velasco out of Philippines, BI confirms
MANILA, Philippines — Fformer House Speaker Lord Allan Velasco has not returned from abroad with yet no cases filed against him, the Bureau of Immigration (BI) confirmed on Tuesday, September 29.
Velasco is among the subjects of the National Bureau of Investigation's probe looking into the allegations of Velasco's former security aide, Rodulfo Gracioso Jr.
The former Marinduque representative has not been issued a hold departure order or other derogatory record that would have prevented him from leaving the country,
Velasco cleared immigration controls without any legal impediment to his departure, the immigration bureau said, citing travel records. It, however, refused to bare more details.
"The BI cannot disclose further details concerning an individual's immigration records due to data privacy concerns," the bureau said.
A hold departure order is a court-issued directive that prevents a person covered by the order from leaving the Philippines while the restriction remains in effect.
"The Bureau remains committed to the consistent enforcement of immigration laws and policies while ensuring the proper protection and confidentiality of personal information," it added.
NBI Director Melvin Matibag separately said Tuesday that Velasco left the country on August 30 and had yet to return. Matibag said immigration records initially showed that Velasco was expected to return on September 14.
His departure therefore preceded the public emergence in late September of allegations by Gracioso, a dismissed police officer, involving purported cash deliveries to Vice President Sara Duterte he made for Velasco .
NBI looking into cash delivery claims
The confirmation of Velasco's whereabouts comes as the NBI investigates allegations contained in Gracioso's sworn affidavit. The bureau has said it plans to invite Velasco and other individuals named in the affidavit to hear their side.
The Philippine National Police said Gracioso had been detailed as a security officer or staff member of Velasco, although it did not immediately specify the period of his assignment.
Gracioso alleged that, on Velasco's instructions, he delivered suitcases containing cash to Duterte, former President Rodrigo Duterte and Davao City Rep. Paolo "Pulong" Duterte. He claimed he made more than 20 deliveries to the vice president totaling more than P2 billion and also alleged delivering more than P1 billion to the former president.
The allegations are being investigated by the NBI.
Velasco's camp has denied Gracioso's allegations, describing them as fabricated and inconsistent with verifiable events. Duterte has likewise denied knowing Gracioso or receiving money from him.

items.title: Sara Duterte trial recap, Sept. 29: Baste Duterte on the stand
items.summary: Davao City Mayor Baste Duterte testified at the impeachment trial of his sister, Vice President Sara Duterte, on Tuesday, September 29, saying he had no direct knowledge of the city's 19 contracts with a firm declared as a business interest in her SALN.
items.body_text:
Sara Duterte trial recap, Sept. 29: Baste Duterte on the stand
MANILA, Philippines — Davao City Mayor Baste Duterte testified at the impeachment trial of his sister, Vice President Sara Duterte, on Tuesday, September 29, saying he had no direct knowledge of the city's 19 contracts with a firm declared as a business interest in her SALN.
The direct and cross-examination of the vice president's brother came down to one main question on GenCorp Industries Inc.: Was there a conflict of interest when the Davao City government awarded it contracts, all while his sister was vice president?
On that question, the mayor repeatedly told the court he could only answer based on the record, as he had not personally reviewed contracts with the firm. Baste said it was the city's bids and awards committee that evaluated GenCorp and that an aide signed the contracts under delegated authority.
He said he was not aware of his sister's business interests because, in his words, "we simply do not discuss this."
A hypothetical, however, surfaced during the proceedings, when Presiding Officer Sen. Chiz Escudero asked whether the mayor would have allowed any award to GenCorp had he known his sister was a stockholder.
"I would not allow it," Baste said.
From 2022 to 2026, Davao City awarded GenCorp 19 food and catering contracts, 15 of them through small value procurement, which does not require public bidding. None were entered into while the vice president herself was the city's mayor.
GenCorp's ties to the vice president exist only on her statement of assets, liabilities and net worth (SALN), which lists her as a stockholder. The corporate records of the company, however, as the Securities and Exchange Commission has shared with the court, do not list Duterte as such.
Escudero said on Monday that this discrepancy has yet to be reconciled.
Here are the three highlights from today's proceedings.
1. No knowledge of GenCorp, but a business partner of a GenCorp stockholder
Under direct questioning by prosecution counsel Theodore Te, the Davao mayor testified he had no personal knowledge of GenCorp before the company was brought up in the impeachment trial.
The mayor however also confirmed that Jaime T. Cruz, GenCorp's major stockholder, is his business partner in another company whose 2026 corporate filing also lists his brother Paolo Duterte.
Duterte said he never discussed GenCorp with Cruz and did not know of Cruz's stake in it.
Sen. Risa Hontiveros asked Baste to describe Cruz's relationship with the Dutertes.
"Maybe not entirely the family, but he's a friend of my father. He's a known businessman in Davao," the mayor said.
Hontiveros said that made the relationship a "close" one.
2. "The witness is not the one on trial"
Escudero repeatedly pressed prosecutors to connect their questions to the article at hand, as "the witness is not the one on trial here."
Sens. Alan Peter Cayetano, JV Ejercito, Bong Go and Joel Villanueva used their turns to argue that a mayor cannot check every single document he signs.
Sen. Ping Lacson noted that the mayor "never denied anything" and asked whether his lawyers had told him of the Arias doctrine, which lets office heads rely on subordinates in good faith.
Sen. Erwin Tulfo asked whether the mayor would look into the contracts himself.
That produced a non-committal answer from the vice president's brother.
"Well, as long as my sister's name, the vice president's name was not on the contract then there's nothing," Baste replied.
3. No answer required
Escudero announced today the court's ruling on the prosecution's request for admission on some 104 items pertaining to her and her husband's bank and tax records.
The court sided with the defense and ruled Duterte does not have to answer the prosecution's 104-item request for admission, citing her right against self-incrimination.
"The prosecution cannot shift its burden of proof to respondent through the simple expedience of a request for admission," Escudero said.

items.title: Heroic teenagers stop drifting school bus after driver passes out
items.summary: Four Pennsylvania high school students brought their drifting school bus to a stop after the driver suffered a medical emergency on the ride home.
items.body_text:
The bus, carrying Hollidaysburg Area School District students in Blair County, had just dropped off 10 junior high pupils on Sept. 17 when it started moving again, 12th-grader Skyla Horton told the Altoona Mirror. Her sister was the last one off.
Horton said the bus had been shaking the whole time it was stopped. Instead of turning at the corner, the driver kept going straight as his head began to bob.
Tenth-grader Alexis Smith, seated near the front, ran to the driver's seat after 12th-grader Travis Zerby told her to hit the brake. She said she first had to shove the gear shifter up, then held the foot brake down.
Smith checked the driver's pulse, which she found weak, and was starting to move him out of his seat when he came to. She kept monitoring his pulse and breathing until medics arrived, according to local broadcaster WTAJ, which published footage of the incident on Sept. 28.
Horton pulled the parking brake and opened the doors for air, while another student opened the rear door to get passengers off. Zerby radioed the bus operator, Fullington Bus Co., and 10th-grader Jenna Anderson called 911.
Smith told WTAJ she missed the first moments because she was texting, until her best friend pulled her out of her seat and told her to get to the driver.
Classroom training pays off
Smith and Horton credited Alisha Clingerman, their health and medical science teacher at the Greater Altoona Career and Technology Center, with teaching them how to act in an emergency.
The driver has since recovered, been medically cleared to drive and returned to his regular route, according to WTAJ.
Hollidaysburg Area Senior High School Principal Breanne Venios reviewed footage from the bus and said every student involved deserved credit. "Not one cellphone was out recording," she told the Mirror.
Venios said the students listened and followed instructions, which she tied to the bus emergency drills they practice. School leaders commended all the junior high and high school students on board for staying calm and working together.

items.title: Vietnamese student clinches top 3 spot in world's largest Chinese-language competition
items.summary: A Vietnamese high school student in the northern province of Lang Son won the Asian championship and placed among the world's top three at the Chinese Bridge competition.
items.body_text:
Do Tue Anh, 18, is a 12th-grade student in the Chinese-language program at the Chu Van An High School for the Gifted.
Competing against 124 others from some 100 countries and territories at the Chinese Bridge competition on Sept. 22, she achieved one of the best results by a Vietnamese student since the competition changed its format in 2020.
Anh first became interested in Chinese as a child while watching "Journey to the West" with her grandparents.
She could not understand why the Chinese characters on the screen were "so complicated," but they fascinated her.
Growing up in Lang Son, where her family’s business near the border gate brought her into regular contact with Chinese people, she gradually became interested in learning the language.
In ninth grade, she seriously started learning Chinese with the goal of gaining admission to a specialized Chinese class.
She says pronunciation was the hardest part at first particularly because she often confused the first and fourth tones.
There were characters whose meanings she understood and could write correctly but could not pronounce accurately, leaving listeners confused.
To improve, she worked through passages in HSK Chinese proficiency test preparation materials, practiced speaking with Vietnamese and Chinese friends, and used AI tools to correct her mistakes.
Her efforts paid off, and she gained admission to the Chu Van An High School for the Gifted with the highest entrance score among candidates applying for its Chinese-language program.
But unlike that goal-driven decision, the one to enter the Chinese Bridge competition came almost by chance following encouragement from her mother and homeroom teacher.
She had less than two months to prepare for the national round in May, which included a written test and question-and-answer section, speech, and talent performance.
She was pleasantly surprised to win first prize, which fetched her a place in the international competition in Tianjin, China, in September.
The international competition lasted about two weeks and consisted of four elimination rounds that narrowed the field first to 30 contestants and then 15, followed by the selection of continental champions and finally the world champion.
Each round comprised of question-and-answer sessions, debates, speeches, and talent performances.
Anh asked former Chinese Bridge contestants for study materials and spent as much time as possible practicing with her teacher.
"I had to study on the bus and even late at night after rehearsals," she says.
For her, the hardest part was the multiple-choice section in the final, in which questions appeared on a computer screen and contestants had to answer immediately after the host finished reading them.
The topics included astronomy, science and technology, classical poetry, and traditional Chinese medicine.
Anh initially answered several questions incorrectly. After a few moments when she "panicked and lost my composure," she looked toward the audience and saw her parents and teacher cheering her on. She gradually calmed down.
"I realized I couldn’t change the questions I’d already got wrong, so I needed to focus on the ones that came next," she says.
She was particularly fond of the talent round.
She performed yangge, a traditional Chinese folk dance commonly seen during festivals and known for its lively style.
Before the competition, she spent several days in Hanoi taking lessons from an instructor before practicing on her own, sometimes until 1 a.m.
For the debate round, she and four other continental champions were placed on the same team. They competed against a team made up of Chinese students and winners from the previous year’s competition.
The motion was whether social media brings people closer together or drives them further apart.
Anh’s team argued that it brings people closer.
Each member had around 30 seconds to present an argument while the team had a total of 180 seconds to rebut the opponents.

items.title: Thai students spared from Australia's ban on bringing family members
items.summary: Thai students will not be affected by Australia's latest visa restrictions banning most international students from bringing family members with them, Australian authorities have confirmed, as Canberra seeks to deepen cooperation with Thailand in trade, migration and regional security.
items.body_text:
Matt Thistlethwaite, Australia's Assistant Minister for Foreign Affairs and Trade and Assistant Minister for Immigration, made the announcement last week during a two-day official visit to Thailand.
Speaking in Bangkok on Sept. 23, Thistlethwaite said Thailand had been excluded from several new migration restrictions because of the close ties between the two countries, the Bangkok Post reported.
He said Thai students would not be subject to the new restrictions, with Thailand among ASEAN and Pacific countries exempted from several of the measures.
"There's no restrictions on Thai people coming to study in Australia, bringing their family members as well. We're very welcoming of Thai students coming to Australia to study at our universities and technical colleges, and it's been a growing relationship that we're happy to foster into the future," he said, as seen in a transcript published on the Department of Foreign Affairs and Trade's website.
"We're seeing more and more Thai students studying at Australian universities, and the Thai diaspora in Australia is about 80,000, and we have the third largest Thai diaspora of any country in the world, and that's something that Australia is very, very proud of, and we want to encourage more of, and the Free Trade Agreement helps us to do that," he said.
Australia recently introduced tightening rules for international students.
Australian Home Affairs Minister Tony Burke announced on Sept. 17 new measures that will limit accompanying family members for most student and post-study work visa holders, crack down on "visa hopping" by tightening rules on switching courses and visa types to extend stays, apply "No Further Stay" conditions to visitor visas, and prioritize visa applications for skilled workers in industries with labor shortages.
The measures form part of Canberra's efforts to bring net overseas migration down from about 290,000 to 225,000 by 2027-28.
Vietnamese students may also be spared from the new restrictions
Brian Quang Dinh, director of consultancy Edunetwork Australia, told Vietnam News Agency in Sydney the key message from the latest changes was that Australia still needs international students and skilled workers but wants to ensure temporary visas are used for their intended purposes.
He said Burke's announcement specified that ASEAN countries and Pacific island nations, along with certain groups of students such as PhD candidates, would be exempt from some of the new restrictions.
Vietnamese passport holders are currently among those allowed to continue bringing family members, subject to applicable conditions, he said.
The restrictions come after the hard-right One Nation party, which has been surging in recent polls, said it would slash the number of temporary migrants by 750,000 over three years to give Australians "breathing space," Reuters reported.
One Nation, which describes its approach as "Australia first" and whose policies have drawn comparisons to those of U.S. President Donald Trump, said it would aim to restrict net overseas migration to 130,000 after the initial three years, with the program expected to be reviewed annually.
Australia’s migration intake, driven largely by international students, backpackers and temporary skilled workers, surged after the country reopened its borders in February 2022 following nearly two years of Covid-19 restrictions, according to Reuters.

items.title: US aircraft carrier with 5,000 crew to call on Phuket
items.summary: Phuket is preparing to welcome 5,000 US navy personnel during a port call by the USS George HW Bush, the second aircraft carrier to visit Thailand after seeing action in the Middle East war.
items.body_text:
Phuket is preparing to welcome 5,000 US navy personnel during a port call by the USS George HW Bush, the second aircraft carrier to visit Thailand after seeing action in the Middle East war.
Pol Col Chatree Chukaew, the Phuket city police chief, held talks on Tuesday with Lu Pham and Robert Robinson, deputy assistant defence attachés at the US Embassy in Thailand, to discuss arrangements for the scheduled visit from Oct 4-9.
Participants discussed co-operation and security arrangements for the visiting sailors during their time on the island. Thai authorities advised US personnel to respect and comply with Thai laws during their stay.
The USS George HW Bush left left Norfolk, Virginia, on March 31, 2026 and was deployed to the Arabian Sea to support operations in the US Central Command region during the conflict with Iran.
The aircraft carrier, with about 4,800 personnel, will be accompanied by the USS Delbert D Black (DDG-119), an Arleigh Burke-class guided-missile destroyer carrying about 320 personnel.
The visit of the carrier comes just a month after a port call in Pattaya in Chon Buri by the USS Abraham Lincoln, also carrying about 5,000 personnel.
The five-day visit was almost incident-free and helped promote a new image of Pattaya as a diverse destination, rather than being mainly about “nightlife and beer bars”, said Pattaya mayor Poramet Ngampichet.
The visit was believed to have pumped about 100 million baht into the local economy, he said.

items.title: 5,600 delayed bags, 330 stalled flights prompt THAI apology
items.summary: Thai Airways International’s (THAI) mishandling of passenger luggage and flight delays caused by flooding have severely damaged Thailand’s image and undermined confidence in its tourism sector, Tourism and Sports Minister Surasak Phancharoenworakul said on Tuesday.
items.body_text:
Thai Airways International’s (THAI) mishandling of passenger luggage and flight delays caused by flooding have severely damaged Thailand’s image and undermined confidence in its tourism sector, Tourism and Sports Minister Surasak Phancharoenworakul said on Tuesday.
Although flooding prevented some staff from commuting normally, the primary cause of the disruption was the airline’s lack of operational readiness and management preparedness, Mr Surasak said.
The minister added that he had personally encountered the problems while returning to Thailand from Japan on a Thai Airways flight.
Torrential rain and flooding in Bangkok over the weekend caused delays involving about 5,600 pieces of luggage and 330 Thai Airways flights, after hundreds of employees were stranded at home and unable to report to work at the country’s two main international airports, Suvarnabhumi and Don Mueang.
The flag carrier said on Tuesday that it aimed to clear the baggage backlog within three days. It had also ordered a 30% reduction in daily flights to allow operations to reset and improve punctuality. A compensation claim process has been opened for affected passengers.
Thai Airways chief apologises
Thai Airways chief executive Chai Eamsiri said the airline’s initial impact assessment had been inaccurate. Flooding prevented about 300 ground staff and specialised personnel from reporting to work, he said during a press conference, while apologising to passengers for the inconvenience.
The airline has about 500 ground staff but was short of 200 to 300 workers during the disruption. Its normal schedule of around 110 flights a day was cut by 30% to help manage the remaining flights and improve on-time performance after almost all flights were delayed, Mr Chai said.
Luggage piled up on the second floor of Suvarnabhumi airport’s passenger terminal after overflowing the conveyor belts on Tuesday. (Photo: Nutthawat Wichieanbut)
Mr Surasak said the problems may have stemmed from the airline assigning staff to serve other carriers under its ground-handling contracts to avoid contractual penalties. This, he said, resulted in the most severe delays affecting Thai Airways' own passengers.
He also criticised the airline for failing to take proactive action despite receiving offers of assistance from several agencies. The national carrier did not provide food or accommodation for military personnel deployed by the Defence Ministry to help clear the baggage backlog, forcing the soldiers to return to their units for meals.
"Every agency tried to step in and help, yet there was no positive response or cooperation from Thai Airways," Mr Surasak said. "I believe Thai Airways executives need to adopt a more proactive approach.
If they feel their term is ending and are unwilling to resolve these issues, they should consider resigning so that others who are truly committed can step in to manage the situation."
Thai Airways brought in three other delivery providers, including Thailand Post and its existing service provider, to help distribute baggage. Airports of Thailand (AOT) assisted with space allocation, while the Royal Thai Air Force, the Defence Ministry and Thai Airways’ headquarters staff provided additional personnel.
Chai: Initial assessment had not been accurate
Deputy Transport Minister Siripong Angkasakulkiat issued a blunt warning.
“If Thai Airways chooses not to look after its passengers, the business repercussions and damage will ultimately rebound on the company itself,” he said.

items.title: Ratchaburi prepares for evacuations as Mae Klong River rises
items.summary: Ratchaburi municipality on Tuesday alerted residents to be on standby for evacuation and ordered schools and childcare centres to close in the face of an imminent threat of major flooding from the rising Mae Klong River.
items.body_text:
Ratchaburi municipality on Tuesday alerted residents to be on standby for evacuation and ordered schools and childcare centres to close in the face of an imminent threat of major flooding from the rising Mae Klong River.
City mayor Sakchai Pisanpol advised communities along the river to start moving personal belongings and valuables to high ground and vehicles to safe parking areas provided by the municipality and Muang police station.
The warning was issued as the Mae Klong continued to rise and looked set to overflow after upstream Mae Klong Dam in Kanchanaburi increased the discharge rate beyond a critical point.
The last devastating flood in Muang district of Ratchaburi was in 1996 and the municipality anticipated a serious flood this time, he said, while asking people not to panic and to keep updated on the situation.
All schools and child daycares run by the municipality were ordered to close for the week.
The Mae Klong runs through the city of Ratchaburi before entering Samut Songkhram.
The dam began releasing 1,900 cubic metres of water per second (cm/s) at 1pm and expected to increase it to 2,500 cm/s, according to Regional Irrigation Office 13, the operator.
A discharge of 1,500 cm/s is considered a critical flood point for people living downstream. It has already been exceeded.
Its first major flood victim could be Ban Pong, a commercial district town in Ratchaburi.
However, the latest information posted by Ban Pong municipality on its Facebook page was a retirement celebration, with smiles all round, on Tuesday. "Please update the (water) situation," a woman with the Facebook name of Nu Nu wrote.
Samut Songkhram municipal workers and volunteers have been building sandbag barriers along the river's edge and at key state offices in preparation for the expected flood when the massive volume of water reaches Muang district.
The office also warned the flood outlook could be worsened by high tides in the Gulf of Thailand, which cause rivers flowing into it to back up.

items.title: Could vanish by 2036: India races to save shrinking island with artificial reefs
items.summary: KARIYACHALLI, Sept 29 — Under a blazing sun, workers crouch on a shrinking island off India’s southern coast...
items.body_text:
KARIYACHALLI, Sept 29 — Under a blazing sun, workers crouch on a shrinking island off India’s southern coast, threading bright green seagrass shoots onto wooden frames before anchoring them onto the ocean floor.
Restoration work on Kariyachalli island hopes to rebuild its natural defences with artificial reefs, transplanted corals and seagrass meadows, in a bid to slow erosion and protect the mainland from surging seas.
“If you are not able to provide that resilience, you are absolutely at the mercy of vulnerabilities of storm surges, cyclonic storms or sea-level rise and also erosion,” senior state official Supriya Sahu told AFP.
AFP travelled by boat to the protected island after being granted exclusive access by the foreign ministry.
Kariyachalli, which is part of a chain of 21 islands in southern Tamil Nadu state, has lost more than 80 per cent of its landmass over the past half century and could disappear entirely by 2036 if erosion is left unchecked.
Government estimates show Kariyachalli shrank from 20.85 hectares in 1969 to just 3.14 hectares last year.
The coral reefs in the Gulf of Mannar, where Kariyachalli and other islands are located, also play a vital role in softening the impact of natural disasters, such as the 2004 Indian Ocean tsunami.
More than 8,000 people were killed in Tamil Nadu during the tsunami, but marine scientists say these ecosystems acted as a crucial natural barrier and prevented a much larger disaster from happening.
Falling reef cover
“This was because these tiny islands, seagrass and coral beds absorb the impact,” said K. Diraviya Raj, an associate professor at the Suganthi Devadason Marine Research Institute.
The Gulf of Mannar is among Asia’s richest marine environments, home to coral reefs, endangered dugongs and hundreds of fish species.
But decades of human activity and climate change have steadily weakened the ecosystem.
Coral mining in the 1960s and 1970s severely damaged reefs around the islands. Pollution, over-fishing and coral bleaching caused by warming seas have also added pressure.
Around Kariyachalli, reef cover fell from roughly 500 hectares in 2005 to 197 hectares in 2021.
The restoration, part of a US$4.79 million (RM19.55 million) state conservation programme, includes the deployment of about 8,500 artificial reef modules around the island.
The bulky structures, each weighing several tonnes, are being lowered into carefully selected locations around Kariyachalli.
Designed using data on seabed conditions, currents and wave patterns, they are intended to break the force of incoming waves while creating new surfaces for corals to colonise.
Experts are also transplanting corals and restoring seagrass meadows that help stabilise sediments and provide nursery grounds for marine life.
The deployment phase is expected to finish by the end of September, after which the site will be monitored for at least four years.
For local residents, the project offers a chance to earn some extra money.
Marine heatwaves
Among them is saltpan worker Devkani, 47, who travels 25 minutes by boat from the mainland to prepare seagrass frames.
“We had to borrow loans earlier at high interest rates to make ends meet during lean months at saltpans,” she told AFP.
“But this year because of this sea-based work, we didn’t have to.”
Though there have been some strides, scientists acknowledge that warming oceans have created significant challenges to reef restoration.
A severe bleaching incident hit the region in 2024, killing large numbers of corals and raising questions about whether restoration efforts can keep pace with climate change.
Researcher Raj argued that the worsening outlook makes intervention even more necessary.
“What we are doing is restoring corals to keep the biomass intact,” he said.
“So, in a way corals will adapt themselves for this deteriorating scenario of changing climatic conditions and will survive to form the future reef.”

items.title: ‘If we can’t sell oil, no one else will’: Iran threatens regional infrastructure as Hormuz talks stall
items.summary: TEHRAN, Sept 29 — Iran today threatened to attack infrastructure around the Middle East, intensifying its rhetoric...
items.body_text:
TEHRAN, Sept 29 — Iran today threatened to attack infrastructure around the Middle East, intensifying its rhetoric as it awaits a formal response from Washington on a new plan to reopen the Strait of Hormuz.
US President Donald Trump has already dismissed the proposal from Tehran, but Iran’s foreign minister said yesterday that he was expecting a formal response from American officials in the coming day.
Fighting has subsided in recent weeks, though Tehran has continued to target ships in the strait, with Washington falling back on an economic pressure campaign instead of further military action.
Iran’s chief negotiator Mohammad Bagher Ghalibaf today threatened new attacks, saying no infrastructure in the region would be safe if his country’s security was not guaranteed.
“In a region where we cannot sell oil, no one else will sell oil either; or if our security is not guaranteed, no infrastructure will remain safe,” Ghalibaf, who is also Iran’s parliament speaker, said according to video released by state TV.
Iranian Foreign Minister Abbas Araghchi said he expected a formal answer from the US today to Tehran’s proposal, state media reported.
Iran has maintained a blockade on commercial shipping through Hormuz since the war began in late February with US-Israeli strikes on the Islamic republic.
The shipping route carried a fifth of the world’s oil and liquefied natural gas before the conflict began.
The US military has been maintaining a counterblockade of Iran’s ports in an effort to prevent Tehran from exporting oil.
Conditions
Araghchi said late yesterday that Qatari intermediaries “presented ideas, and we discussed them; they are set to raise the matter with the American side once more, after which the final US response will be conveyed to us”.
The top diplomat, who was in New York for the UN General Assembly, said “the Qataris hope this will be done by tomorrow”.
“The current focus is solely on the Strait of Hormuz, and the reopening of the strait is contingent upon the fulfilment of certain conditions that we have communicated to the other side,” he added.
Last week, discussions were held in New York between Araghchi and US envoys Steve Witkoff and Jared Kushner.
As a precondition for ending its blockade, Iran is demanding a seven-day ceasefire across the Middle East, including in Lebanon, where its ally Hezbollah is regularly bombarded by Israel.
It is also demanding the unfreezing of Iranian assets abroad, the lifting of sanctions on its oil sector and an end to the US naval blockade on its ports.
Both sides claim to have control of Hormuz, with the US saying oil is moving through and Tehran insisting the waterway is closed.
Today, Iran’s Revolutionary Guards, the ideological arm of the country’s military, said “the US claim that it remains open is false”.
“Sneaking a few hundred barrels of oil through under the cover of darkness — with transponders turned off and at great cost — does not constitute the strait being open,” said spokesperson Hossein Mohebi.
“A truly open strait is one where, as in the past, at least 125 vessels would pass through daily, transporting a minimum of 20 million barrels of oil and petroleum products.
“Any vessel attempting to pass through sustains damage — either we strike it, or it hits a mine,” he added. — AFP

items.title: ‘Gift from God’: Rain brings relief from Indonesia toxic haze
items.summary: PONTIANAK, Sept 29 — Welcome rain has brought relief to residents of Indonesia’s Pontianak city after weeks...
items.body_text:
PONTIANAK, Sept 29 — Welcome rain has brought relief to residents of Indonesia’s Pontianak city after weeks of exposure to a cloying, toxic haze given off by rampant wildfires on Borneo island.
Fires have torn through vast swathes of peat and forest areas on Borneo and nearby Sumatra island, with the resulting haze drifting also to neighbouring Malaysia and Singapore.
The thick smog had limited outdoor activities in Pontianak, a city of about 700,000 people, with schools forced to shutter and thousands of respiratory cases recorded in the region since last month, according to officials.
Rains in recent days have brought a welcome respite, said homemaker Lilis Suryani, who has been worrying about the effects of the haze on her children’s health.
“After the rain, I immediately felt the difference. The air was better, and the visibility was clearer,” the 43-year-old told AFP.
University student Uray Rosa Febrianti, 23, said that “the rain means a lot... not only to cool the air, but also to give hope that the situation is beginning to improve”.
“I see it as a gift from God.”
Indonesia has deployed firefighters assisted by volunteers across affected areas, and used cloud-seeding and water-bombing, with limited success.
The level of PM2.5 pollution in Pontianak was still more than 23 times the World Health Organization’s safe limit at one point today, according to IQAir, a Switzerland-based monitor.
Earlier this month, levels of PM2.5 in the city were over 100 times the recommended cap.
PM2.5 particles are so small they can enter deep into the lungs and even the bloodstream, with potentially dire consequences for health.
Indonesia regularly battles wildfires during the dry season, which in Borneo typically peaks between July and September.
The fires have intensified this year in part because of the El Nino weather phenomenon, set to be one of the strongest since comparable records began four decades ago.
El Nino typically brings severe drought to Indonesia.
Experts have also pointed to slash-and-burn land-clearing practices that have changed the naturally fire-resistant landscape. — AFP

items.title: AT&T signs over $3 billion fiber deal with Corning as data demand surges
items.body_text:
AT&T signs over $3 billion fiber deal with Corning as data demand surges
Sept 29 : AT&T on Tuesday said it had signed a multi-year deal worth more than $3 billion with Corning to procure fiber and cable, as the telecom giant expands its network to meet surging demand for data.
Corning shares rose 3.3 per cent in premarket trading.
Fiber network build-out has emerged as a critical growth area for the telecom industry as the wireless market matures and internet usage surges.
Growing demand for data-intensive services, including AI workloads, cloud computing and connected devices, is increasing the need for faster, more resilient and scalable fiber networks.
"The average AT&T Fiber household now uses more than 1 terabyte each month, 5x more than in 2016. And that number is expected to keep climbing," AT&T said.
Fiber is also seen as a critical component for telecom companies because it can quickly carry data for services ranging from video calls and movie streaming to AI tools.
The company expects aims to reach 60 million fiber locations by the end of the decade as part of its multi-billion dollar infrastructure expansion.
Its $5.75 billion acquisition of Lumen's fiber business has further expanded its fiber footprint. The company has committed more than $250 billion over five years to strengthen US connectivity infrastructure.

items.title: Japan's fusion energy startup to begin power-on tests at pilot reactor in 2027
items.body_text:
Japan's fusion energy startup to begin power-on tests at pilot reactor in 2027
TOKI, Japan, Sept 29 : Japanese startup Helical Fusion expects to begin preliminary power-on tests at its demonstration fusion reactor in 2027, it said on Tuesday, a step towards its goal of becoming a global leader in commercial nuclear fusion energy.
The company is developing Helix HARUKA, Japan's first integrated pilot reactor using the helical approach to fusion. The pilot facility is designed to demonstrate the feasibility of stable, continuous fusion reactions.
Nuclear fusion involves smashing atoms together at super-high temperatures to generate heat the same way the sun does. It could one day produce enormous amounts of clean power with little radioactive waste, in contrast to today's fission reactors.
Despite global efforts to harness fusion energy, 70 years of research have yet to yield a commercially viable reactor.
Helical Fusion completed a performance test of a high-temperature superconducting (HTS) coil in 2025, replicated the magnetic environment inside a fusion device and achieved a stable current flow under superconducting conditions, in a world first. The result cleared a key hurdle for manufacturing and constructing the integrated demonstration reactor, it said.
Construction of the first spiral coil at the National Institute for Fusion Science (NIFS) site in Toki, central Japan, started early this year and is now largely complete, allowing the company to open the facility to the media.
If the first-stage tests are successful, Helical Fusion said it planned to install a second coil and other major components, including a liquid-metal wall blanket, before conducting power-on tests of the completed integrated facility around 2030.
The company plans to follow HARUKA with HELIX KANATA, a bigger reactor with a net power output of 50 MW, aiming to demonstrate stable and continuous power generation. It plans to begin full-scale investment in the project in the 2030s.
Helical Fusion is the sole private-sector inheritor of the helical fusion technology developed by NIFS, one of the world's largest fusion research facilities. It aims to develop the world's first commercially viable fusion power plant based on the helical design.
Helical Fusion CEO Takaya Taguchi told reporters the company aims to build a commercial power plant as early as the 2040s but said before commercial operations can begin, there are various hurdles to overcome—not only technical ones, but also issues such as cost, safety and construction speed.
Japanese Prime Minister Sanae Takaichi is a strong supporter of the nuclear fusion industry. The government has designated fusion energy as one of 17 strategic sectors and plans to invest 3.1 trillion yen ($19.7 billion) through public and private sector funding by the 2040 financial year.
($1 = 157.0600 yen)

items.body_text:
Goh Jin Hian testifies in false trading trial, says he believed market-making services 'completely legal'
"I was very sensitive to anything wrong being done because of the reputation of the individuals in the board and even to my own reputation," Dr Goh Jin Hian said as he took the stand.
SINGAPORE: Former chief executive officer of investment holding company New Silkroutes Group (NSG) Dr Goh Jin Hian told the court on Tuesday (Sep 29) that he was unfamiliar with the market-making industry when the company engaged designated market maker GTC Group in 2018, but believed its services were "completely legal".
The 57-year-old son of former prime minister Goh Chok Tong also described how he was very sensitive to any wrong being done because of the reputations at stake, including his own.
Dr Goh took the stand in his false trading trial for the second day on Tuesday. He is accused of conspiring with other executives from NSG, a publicly traded company, to push up the share price as the company's business strategy was premised on a high share price.
He is contesting charges of conspiring to create a misleading appearance of NSG's share price, and of "doing things with the purpose of creating a misleading appearance of NSG's share price".
Dr Goh is on trial alongside NSG's former chief corporate officer, 55-year-old Kelvyn Oo Cheong Kwan. They are accused of engaging in the conspiracy, along with market maker Huang Yiwen and former NSG finance director William Teo Thiam Chuan, both of whom have been convicted and sentenced.
Dr Goh told the court that NSG was under "some pressure" to lift a months-long suspension on trading in its shares, which he believed were already thinly traded. Thinly traded securities are financial assets that are difficult to buy or sell without affecting their market price.
When he and NSG met Huang, the sole shareholder and director of GTC Group in February 2018, there was little time to engage a market maker before lifting the trading suspension. 
Market makers refer to financial firms or individuals who keep markets liquid by offering prices at which they will buy and sell an asset. Under SGX rules, designated market makers are required to provide competitive bid and offer quotations to provide for an adequately liquid market.
He also addressed the S$60,000 (US$46,900) monthly fee GTC charged, which he considered high but agreed to after consulting his team.
"I didn't know the market rate, I didn't know the industry at all," he said.
WHY NSG ENGAGED A MARKET MAKER
Dr Goh said he first met Huang in February 2018, in what was their only meeting.
Huang had been introduced to NSG through Teo, after Dr Goh asked the latter if he knew any market makers who could "support shares and prevent Shen killing the price" when the company's trading suspension was lifted.
This referred to NSG's former director and substantial shareholder Lee Soek Shen, whom Dr Goh believed was selling large volumes of his shares, exerting downward pressure on NSG's share price.
Dr Goh testified that he had learnt it was possible to engage a market maker to provide liquidity for NSG's shares and believed it to be "completely legal" to do so.
During their meeting, Huang explained market making to Dr Goh and described GTC Group as a designated market maker on SGX.
According to Dr Goh, Huang said his services could mitigate short-term volatility caused by Mr Lee's selling and, over time, allow NSG's shares to trade towards what Dr Goh considered their fair value.
NSG had requested a trading halt in November 2017, followed by a voluntary suspension of its shares in December while it negotiated acquisitions.
After nearly three months of suspension and just days after announcing three major deals, the company said in February 2018 that its shares would resume trading the following day.
Asked whether he or NSG had tried to meet with other market makers, Dr Goh said he did not know where to find them.

items.title: Iranians stagger under soaring costs of seven months of war
items.summary: LONDON, Sept 29 - Iran's leaders may radiate bullishness in their war with the United States, but life is becoming ever tougher for ordinary citizens unable to afford basic necessities or rent as a US blockade cuts the state's financial lifeline - oil exports.
items.body_text:
Iranians stagger under soaring costs of seven months of war
LONDON, Sept 29 - Iran's leaders may radiate bullishness in their war with the United States, but life is becoming ever tougher for ordinary citizens unable to afford basic necessities or rent as a US blockade cuts the state's financial lifeline - oil exports.
From an engineer forced out of Tehran by high rent to a woman forced to stop smoking because of the price of cigarettes and carers struggling to buy medicines, all areas of daily life are affected.
"I'm forced to sell my items with a very small and negligible profit, yet I can't close my business because then I'd be unemployed," said Behnam Riazi, a restaurant owner interviewed on camera in Tehran.
Riazi cannot raise his prices because his customers cannot pay more - any most anyway buy only necessities now.
How far economic strains may push Iran towards diplomatic compromise is unclear, as it tightens its own stranglehold on Gulf energy exports through the Strait of Hormuz, driving up oil and gas prices in the US and around the world.
ECONOMIC MISERY MAY SPUR DIPLOMACY
However, the latest burst of diplomacy was partly spurred by economic strains, US, Middle Eastern and Iranian sources said last week. Iranian officials have repeatedly expressed fears of unrest, and cracked down ruthlessly on rumblings of dissent.
In January, over a month before the US and Israel began their war on Iran, authorities killed thousands of demonstrators exasperated by years of cumulative economic distress.
But now, all those Reuters spoke to said they had too many daily worries to think about protesting.
Hediyeh, a housewife in her 60s in northern Iran, survives on her husband's civil service pension. She can barely afford medicine or even the adult diapers needed by her elderly mother, who has Alzheimer's disease.She wanted to buy her grandson a new bag for his first day at school this autumn, but it cost five or six times what she had expected, and in the end she could only buy him a notebook and pencils.
Like most of the Iranians Reuters interviewed by phone or messaging app, she did not want to be identified, fearing punishment for speaking to foreign media.
A.J., a teacher who asked only to be identified by his initials, also said he cannot always afford the medicine his mother needs.
He has already moved in with his mother and siblings in a northern village, leaving Tehran after schools moved online because of the war, but fears he will no longer be able to afford to return if in-person teaching resumes.
In Sanandaj, capital of Kurdistan province, 34-year-old psychotherapist Nazanin has given up smoking because of the cost after having previously found it impossible to do so, she said.
Those who can afford to bypass the usual ways of obtaining goods or services through the black market are finding it has become more pervasive, though the cost has gone up.
One man said he had paid $200 in hard currency to a surgeon to get around the bureaucratic process needed for an operation.
Another said police requests for bribes were growing more frequent, and that he had had to pay more than before after being stopped at a checkpoint without identification papers.
JOBS BEING CUT IN PRIVATE SECTOR
An architect, who only gave his initials A.A., said even wealthier Iranians were cutting back: "All of them have become poor relative to the lifestyle they used to have."
His car had a puncture last week and he is having to drive on a spare tyre for the two weeks it takes to get a cheap replacement; he can no longer afford those available immediately.
He worries that Iran is heading for fuel shortages, which could disrupt supply chains and cause wider economic havoc.
Already, the war is causing heavy job losses across the private sector.

items.title: Ousted Guinea-Bissau leader to run in December election, source says
items.summary: BISSAU, Sept 29 - Deposed Guinea-Bissau President Umaro Sissoco Embalo plans to return to the country on October 4 to run for the presidency in an election scheduled for December, a source familiar with the matter told Reuters.
items.body_text:
Ousted Guinea-Bissau leader to run in December election, source says
BISSAU, Sept 29 - Deposed Guinea-Bissau President Umaro Sissoco Embalo plans to return to the country on October 4 to run for the presidency in an election scheduled for December, a source familiar with the matter told Reuters.
• Embalo was toppled in a military coup last November, shortly before results from presidential and legislative elections were due to be announced.
• Senior army officers suspended the electoral process and installed Major-General Horta Inta-a as transitional president.
• The military authorities later scheduled new presidential and legislative elections on December 6 this year.
• Embalo's campaign organisation has not yet been finalised, one source close to Embalo said, adding that the military-led government had assured the former president that he is "welcome" to return. A government spokesperson did not respond to a request for comment.
• Embalo has been outside the country since the coup last year, fleeing to Senegal and then the Republic of Congo. Reuters could not establish his current whereabouts.
• Guinea-Bissau approved a new constitution in a referendum in August that expanded presidential powers and changed electoral rules. Among other provisions, it requires presidential candidates to have lived continuously in the country for the preceding five years. It was unclear how that provision might affect Embalo's candidacy.
• Guinea-Bissau, a small Portuguese-speaking West African country, has a long history of military coups and is a transit hub for cocaine bound for Europe. REUTERS

items.title: Questioning Russian threat to Europe is irresponsible, Germany's top diplomat says in Slovakia
items.summary: Sept 29 - Russia's imperialism is the greatest threat to Europe and to question that is irresponsible, Germany's foreign minister said on Tuesday in Slovakia, where the prime minister has criticised the West's approach on Ukraine.
items.body_text:
Questioning Russian threat to Europe is irresponsible, Germany's top diplomat says in Slovakia
Sept 29 - Russia's imperialism is the greatest threat to Europe and to question that is irresponsible, Germany's foreign minister said on Tuesday in Slovakia, where the prime minister has criticised the West's approach on Ukraine.
"The greatest threat to the freedom of our continent comes from Moscow. The greatest danger to Europe is (Russian President Vladimir) Putin's belligerent imperialism," said German Foreign Minister Johann Wadephul as he met Slovak counterpart Juraj Blanar.
"To question these facts is not only lacking in solidarity, but it would be simply irresponsible."
Slovakia, led by Prime Minister Robert Fico's leftist-nationalist government, has questioned the European Union and NATO's reaction to the war that followed Russia's full-scale invasion of Ukraine in 2022.
Fico has maintained warm relations with Moscow, including meetings with Putin, and battled the EU over measures to end Russian oil and gas supplies, which Bratislava still needs.
This month, Fico criticised unnamed Western politicians for wanting to stoke conflict between NATO and Russia after a "failed" strategy to defeat Moscow.
He also said Europe was closer than ever to war and that he wanted to keep Slovakia out of conflict.
He said in a television interview at the weekend that he did not believe partners would send troops to help Slovakia in a war. Fico has said he would prefer neutrality, but he was bound by NATO membership.
WADEPHUL SAYS OBSTRUCTION IN BRUSSELS IS SELF-DEFEATING
Slovak opposition parties have criticised Fico for calling into question Slovakia's commitment to NATO collective defence.
Wadephul said on Tuesday that states needed to rely on security guarantees, and that casting doubt on NATO's deterrence capability put "all of us at risk".
He also said the EU had already been through "systemic obstructionism" by Hungary under former prime minister Viktor Orban, whose 16-year rule ended in election defeat earlier this year. Orban had often held up EU measures against Russia.
Slovakia earlier this year opted out — together with Hungary and the Czech Republic — of an EU loan for Ukraine, and has delayed sanctions against Russia in the past due to energy policies.
Wadephul said "blockades" in Brussels weakened the EU.
"Ultimately, it harms the party doing the blocking most of all," he said. REUTERS
